📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A upcoming feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

With Claude Ship, confirmed in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic noted. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

Industry observers note that “Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic noted. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

According to recent reports, the upcoming feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise plans. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic stated, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

Sources indicate that PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

It has been revealed that as a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic mentioned.

“It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic stated it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic stated in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz said the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

Industry observers note that also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

Recent findings suggest that “But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he said. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz said he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the organization and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he remarked.

Developer platforms overall are adapting to the newly introduced state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

Sources indicate that individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “users won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

Sources indicate that still, that depends on the number of PRs owners are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the newly introduced PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

It has been revealed that anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

  • Given that, the world’s largest semiconductor tech giant possibly wishes its biggest problem were software-related.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has had its share of drama lately, with the ousting and sudden un-ousting of CEO Jensen Huang after it was discovered he’d had multiple affairs, including one that involved an alleged member of a Chinese spy network. The fallout from the revelations was so significant that some worried Huang’s fate could be a major disruptor to the health of international markets and the future of the entire AI industry.

Given that, the world’s largest semiconductor tech giant possibly wishes its biggest problem were software-related. But that won’t be much comfort to PC consumers affected by a software bug in Nvidia’s graphics driver that has caused some to experience excessive writes to their solid-state drives.

The concern began popping up in mid-November as posts on Nvidia’s support forums, as well as on Reddit and sites like HardForum, reported seeing as much as 30GB to 70GB of data per hour written to their SSDs. These types of drives wear down rapidly over months of such use.

Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment and hasn’t made any public statements on the concern, but did acknowledge it in a hotfix and subsequent software enhancement for its Windows 11 GeForce Game Ready Driver 621.40, where it stated under Fixed General Bugs, “Excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background.” The driver that appeared to have caused the problems was released on Nov. 12.Some tech experts on social media had been suggesting rolling back to older graphics drivers before the hotfixes were released and warned that letting the problem go unchecked could cause an SSD to eventually fail.

Described by WCCF Tech as “a hotfix for the hotfix,” the fresh upgrade appears to fix the glitch in ways that the previous fix did not.

In a recent development, nvidia’s software problem closely mirrors an issue AMD had with its own Adrenalin Edition graphics software just weeks ago. As of Nov. 18, AMD was still making tweaks to its graphics software to iron out any lingering problems.

PCGamer offered a way to check if your PC is affected by the excess writing problem.

According to recent reports, open Task Manager, click on the Details tab and right-click on the columns at the top to select “I/O write bytes” as one of your Task Manager columns. By doing that, you can see if the file “NVDisplay.Container.exe” is writing a huge amount of data to your data drive.

If that’s the case, you should upgrade immediately to Nvidia’s latest drivers for the fix. In fact, it might be a good idea to update whether you’re experiencing high write rates or not, just to be safe.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Along with the general sensor, processor, and battery upgrades, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 introduced Audio Intelligence, a upcoming set of features that allows the watch to listen in on conversations.
  • Siri Recap generates summaries of what you’ve discussed throughout the day, while Live Rewind gives you a transcript of the last 15 seconds of audio in case you missed something.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that no, your phone isn’t listening to you. But what about your Apple Watch? I’ve been testing new Audio Intelligence features that record conversations around me, and despite how disturbing it may sound to have your smartwatch listening and taking notes of your entire day, the reality has been a lot more mundane.

Along with the general sensor, processor, and battery upgrades, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 introduced Audio Intelligence, a upcoming set of features that allows the watch to listen in on conversations.

Siri Recap generates summaries of what you’ve discussed throughout the day, while Live Rewind gives you a transcript of the last 15 seconds of audio in case you missed something.

It’s similar functionality as AI-powered recording pins like Plaud or Amazon’s Bee, but within the context of your smartwatch and without the additional cost or subscription.

According to recent reports, and it’s completely optional. You have to first opt-in to the features to activate them, then choose to turn the feature you want on whenever you want to start using it. Then you can leave it on all day, set it on a schedule or toggle it manually whenever you need it. If you’re like me and forget that it’s on, you get reminders that it’s still listening or to check your recaps.

The fact that you have so much control over whether you use it and how much helped ease the creepy factor for me, but there’s still everyone else to consider.

Beyond a barely audible chime when I double-click the Digital Crown to activate Live Rewind, there’s no way to alert others that the feature is in use and that whoever’s in earshot is inadvertently getting roped into my little experiment as well. Other wearables like smart glasses have an indicator light on the front to alert spectators when they’re recording video.

In a recent development, apple has built-in privacy safeguards for the audio, how it’s processed and then deleted. I’ve broken all that down in a separate Audio Intelligence FAQ. This is about what it’s like to use it in the wild.

According to recent reports, I’ve been testing Audio Intelligence in the WatchOS 27.3 (and iOS) public beta for two weeks. Because this isn’t the final version (Apple says it will release publicly later this year), consider this a sneak preview.

It has been revealed that let’s get Live Rewind out of the way because there’s not a lot to say about it. Whether from a lack of muscle memory (or usefulness), I’ve had to go out of my way to remember the feature exists.

Recent findings suggest that I figured it’d come in handy for those “come again?” moments during conversations, but the reality is that it’s just easier to ask someone to repeat what they noted than remember to double-press the Digital Crown at just the right moment. I can see it being more useful when you’re listening to a presentation or other event.

It has been revealed that fifteen seconds go by a lot faster than I expect and by the time I realize something might be worth revisiting, the person has moved on with the conversation. I either missed what I intended to get or just captured the silence after.

Siri Recap has been more useful, though it’s still hit-or-miss. The feature gives you high-level summaries of what it heard — it doesn’t provide a transcript to review, and it doesn’t identify who said what. It shines brightest during dedicated meetings when there’s a single conversation to follow rather than a jumble of unrelated discussions.

One success story: I was moderating the chat for our iPhone Duo live folding test on YouTube while Matthew Murray, CNET’s lab director, answered viewer questions on the stream.

I thought I’d caught the gist of what he was saying, but the typing must’ve distracted me more than I realized because I was pleasantly surprised to learn some interesting facts that I’d missed in the Siri Recap, like “Opening a phone 20 times daily over 10 years equals 73,000 folds” or that the “machine runs approximately 22,560 cycles every 24 hours”.

But Siri’s batting average wasn’t always that good, which made it challenging to trust the notes. During a conversation with another mom about car-pool logistics, Siri Recap pulled out action items, like who I was picking up and at what time, which I appreciated, but the information wasn’t accurate. Not only had Siri gotten the names of the kids wrong, it also had me picking up the wrong kid. Clearly, the mental load of figuring out after-school logistics is challenging even for Siri.

Siri can’t handle the messy conversations (and TV shows).

Where things get interesting (and occasionally hilarious) is how Siri discerns what constitutes a conversation and how many topics belong in a single recap.

Siri is generally good at accurately labeling what conversations are about: “Parent-teacher conferences,” “Car-pool logistics,” “Folding phone durability testing.” But rather than keeping them separate, as it should, it sometimes conflates two or even three completely unrelated conversations into a single recap.

I encountered bullet points summarizing a serious conversation with a friend about a medical condition alongside notes about a chaotic (albeit funny) exploding apple cider incident with my kids. The two conversations happened within the same two-hour window, but they were by no means back-to-back.

It’s a good thing Siri Recap leaves out tone and volume cause that last bullet would’ve been in ALL CAPS.

What it did decide was worthy of a standalone recap was a discussion about wedding aims during an episode of Nobody Wants This on Netflix. To be fair, this would’ve absolutely warranted a recap if I’d been discussing my own wedding plans; however, the fact that the “conversation” happened at midnight should’ve tipped off Siri that this was a late-night binge session and not an actual conversation needing to be recapped.

Recent findings suggest that rather than coming away better informed about the crucial conversations I’d had throughout the day, I came away feeling validated by the sheer chaos of it all. The constant whiplash of being pulled in a dozen different directions — bouncing between work, kids, gossip and the occasional sticky beverage crisis — was real and now immortalized (until the recap automatically expires if you don’t choose to save it).

According to recent reports, for now, while novel, neither Siri Recap nor Live Rewind is reason enough to buy (or avoid) the Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. They’re two of our top-rated smartwatches for their fitness, health and other smart features. Audio Intelligence is either an added bonus (it’s free) or something you can ignore altogether.

But if you do decide to venture into this brave newly introduced world of AI notetakers, my suggestion would be to use Siri Recap intentionally rather than leaving it running all day.

It has been revealed that turn it on before a work meeting, a doctor’s appointment or another conversation where you might want a few notes to jog your memory later. Just make sure everyone involved knows it’s enabled and is comfortable with it, and that you’re not relying on it for crucial information.

If the stakes are high, have a backup — whether that’s your own notes or a recording — lest you risk coming home with the wrong kid.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Rick Orford – Nov 25, 2026 at 9:19AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Joby Aviation ›.

Joby Aviation (JOBY -3.13%) and Archer Aviation (ACHR -4.32%) are racing to bring electric air taxis to the Middle East. But Joby appears to have the edge in Dubai after the city declared a newly certified vertiport on Nov. 18, which could carry its first paying passenger before Archer releases in Abu Dhabi. Here's what that could mean for both stocks.

Joby's partnership with Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) gives it a considerable head start in bringing its aircraft to market. Specifically, the manufacturer has exclusive rights to operate air taxi services in Dubai under its agreement, positioning it to establish an early foothold in one of the world's most ambitious transportation markets.

The RTA has also declared the completion and regulatory certification of the Dubai Marina vertiport, a major development because it establishes the first permanent vertiport-to-vertiport electric air-taxi route. And while Joby is the designated operator for this route, commercial operations will still require necessary approvals.

It has been revealed that joby has also mentioned it intends to conduct flight testing with a pilot aboard in Dubai before the end of 2026. While a pilot isn't a customer, successful testing would be a major milestone and could increase the organization's chances of becoming the first major electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft manufacturer to launch a commercial passenger operation.

NYSE · As of 11:17 AM ET 11/25/26.

There are still risks, of course. For one, Joby has yet to prove that its service can operate profitably at scale. On top of that, any delays in certification, production, or customer adoption could delay its plans.

Joby stock also trades at a price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of about 23 times, with investors likely expecting that Joby can successfully launch commercial air taxi operations.

Meanwhile, another company has set its sights on Abu Dhabi, and its ambitions could make this a much closer race than investors expect.

Sources indicate that if Joby gets the first paying passengers in Dubai, Archer could find itself trying to catch up in the Middle East. But that doesn't necessarily mean Archer is losing the race.

Archer has been working closely with Abu Dhabi's government and aviation authorities to get its electric air taxi service off the ground, literally. Its Midnight aircraft, for example, completed its first test flight in Abu Dhabi in July 2025.

It has been revealed that more importantly, Archer has made progress on the regulatory front. Specifically, the UAE's General Civil Aviation Authority moved its Midnight aircraft into a Restricted Type Certificate (RTC) program. That matters because it provides a pathway to limited commercial operations without waiting for full certification.

Archer is also working with Abu Dhabi Aviation as its local operating partner, giving it access to an established aviation operator that can help with the requirements of launching the service.

NYSE · As of 11:17 AM ET 11/25/26.

Today, however, the risk is that Joby beats Archer to commercial operations. If that happens, Archer stock could face near-term pressure as investors think the eVTOL race has been won.

Industry observers note that but like Joby Aviation, Archer faces risks around certification delays, production, and execution. Archer stock also trades at a lofty valuation with a P/S of about 185 times, meaning expectations are high that its Midnight aircraft will become a huge commercial success.

Ultimately, the race between Joby and Archer is more about who can turn its early lead into a sustainable business.

Joby could have the early-mover advantage, potentially boosting its stock while putting pressure on Archer. Then again, a successful Dubai launch could also validate the eVTOL market, benefiting other companies like Archer. Although both stocks face execution risks, the long-term opportunity remains compelling.

If Dubai delivers that first paying passenger, Joby investors will likely come out ahead.

Industry News: Zelda Producers: Ocarina of Time Remake Is a Bridge to the Future

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the last month, I fell in love with a new game that’s actually old.
  • I’m still thinking about (and playing) Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2, even with GTA 6 loaded up at home.
  • Recent findings suggest that I also can’t stop thinking about what a game like this means for Nintendo’s next wave of Switch 2 games, and a future Zelda game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the last month, I fell in love with a new game that’s actually old. It’s happened to me before, but Nintendo’s Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake drove that feeling home in a surprising way. How did Nintendo get me to fall so deeply in love again with a game I’ve already played? And why is it still winning me over, even with Grand Theft Auto 6 here?

I’m still thinking about (and playing) Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2, even with GTA 6 loaded up at home. GTA’s universe overwhelms me, but it also makes me appreciate Ocarina’s focus and clarity. And it’s also another incredible graphics showcase for what the Switch 2 is capable of. Yes, GTA 6 is jaw-dropping. But so are Ocarina’s 60fps vistas and details. Zelda pioneered 3D gaming before GTA ever went 3D.

Recent findings suggest that I also can’t stop thinking about what a game like this means for Nintendo’s next wave of Switch 2 games, and a future Zelda game. Zelda’s previous games became increasingly open world, full of multiplying tasks and larger maps. It can get overwhelming. Ocarina of Time’s focus is smaller, but still tangled and immersive. Can the two concepts feed off each other? Will Ocarina help rethink where the next Zeldas are heading? And, maybe, where other open-world games are heading, too?

At Ocarina’s launch, I met in person with Nintendo’s producers for the remake, Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, to discuss what it all meant and how the remake bridged the gap between the “old Zelda” and “new Zelda.” Aonuma has been a producer for Zelda games since the original Ocarina of Time, and Fujibayashi directed both Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.

For this project, they brought on staffers who’d worked on Tears of the Kingdom, many of them much younger developers.

“In fact, some of them hadn’t even played the original Ocarina of Time on Nintendo 64,” notes Aonuma. “We also saw this as a really interesting opportunity for this younger staff to make discoveries on the course of this project that they could bring forward on future Zelda projects that they might work on as well.”.

There are a lot more subtle visual clues, I found, even than what I remembered in Nintendo’s last two Zelda games.

Industry observers note that “When we were working on Tears of the Kingdom, we had this very high capacity to express all kinds of details and this feeling of immersion in the world, and that’s something I think was a significant influence on the remake,” says Aonuma. “Whether it’s a visual detail that you might spot from a distance that you may not have in the original, that could be something that draws the player in and suddenly gives them the motivation to explore.”.

Sources indicate that what worked wonders, I found, was the quiet, subtle immersion, especially when exploring dungeons or figuring out solutions I’d forgotten decades ago. I had to study the environment for clues.

That’s the magic ingredient: a throughline in the Zelda games that Fujibayashi states is “the idea of exploration and discovery.”.

Fujibayashi appreciates how the visual tools have improved, even since Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom on the original Switch.

“A system that lets you share a high, dense volume of information visually provides upcoming ways of giving clues to the player: They can use their sight to gather the information they need to do some of the puzzle solving,” he notes. “Even if you compare the graphics to Breath of the Wild, it looks slightly more realistic now. And that impacts how we approach puzzle solving and puzzle creation.”.

I think about Grand Theft Auto as the upcoming benchmark for immersion and graphic detail, but I’m also finding that a lot of GTA’s discoveries are made through pop-up interaction graphics that let you know when something can be activated. Ocarina of Time doesn’t always do this. And I also can’t help but wonder: Could the Switch 2 achieve a way to run a new wave of impressive games using optimized graphics, even something on a level like Grand Theft Auto’s latest?

Or, rather, what if Nintendo aims for a latest level of hyper-immersion in its games going forward, learning from Ocarina of Time?

Industry observers note that speaking of immersion, I kind of wish I could hold my Joy-Con up and use it like an ocarina in the fresh game. You can’t, although you can use the controllers to play notes or hum or play a tune into the built-in microphone using your own voice or instrument — something lots of people have been showing off online. But the Joy-Con-as-ocarina idea almost became a reality.

“To be honest, we did briefly think about doing exactly that, but then we also considered how difficult it is to turn the Joy-Con into something that’s going to make a sound that is faithful, and then also how to develop that into the application inside of the game as well,” claims Aonuma. “What we ultimately decided to do instead was to have this audio recognition feature in the software where you can use any instrument that you would like, whether it’s analog or digital, and you can play these themes and have the effect in the game and experience that way.”.

In a recent development, what I’m really hoping for is a Majora’s Mask remake, the second N64 Zelda game that built off Ocarina’s graphics engine. Nintendo could do the same here, although Nintendo wouldn’t answer my questions about Majora’s Mask during my interview.

I’m still unlocking all the little secrets in Ocarina of Time, sinking into the world as I go. And when I play the notes on my Switch, I imagine I’m playing that ocarina. After playing this Zelda game, I wonder what Nintendo could do with that same level of detail for Mario’s return on the Switch 2, almost 10 years after the last new 3D Mario game on the Switch. We might know the answer to that soon enough.

Google has added Wallet integration to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, letting you learn about your spending habits, strategy a budget, maximize credit card rewards, and more with a simple Search.

Starting today, Google revealed, Personal Intelligence for Search is expanding to more apps, including Wallet and Drive. Google can’t move or manage any money, but it can give you tailored, personalized search results about your finances, like showing where you spend the most, identifying recurring subscriptions you might not be aware of, and suggesting which credit card might be best to use for travel. All you have to do is ask in a search.

Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.

This feature comes just over a week after Google introduced Personal Intelligence to Wallet.

Sources indicate that once your Wallet is connected, it takes a few minutes to fully sync. Once it’s finished, you can ask questions through AI mode in Search.

I decided to give it a try for myself, starting off with a simple query: “Based on my spending, what’s a quick way I can save money?” I could have told you one of the primary culprits, but Google happily responded with what I already knew: far too much of my money goes to fast food and coffee.

“You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response mentioned, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

Also: This powerful Gemini setting made my AI results way more personal and accurate.

It has been revealed that when I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. What I didn’t ask for, but it did, was to break down those subscriptions into an easy-to-see chart, complete with the name, price, category, the card it’s being charged to, and the timeframe it usually comes out. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

According to recent reports, since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to Newly introduced York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

Also: Slow Android phone? How to speed it back up in 4 easy steps.

According to recent reports, while Gemini Personal Intelligence can access your Gmail to learn more about your spending, it can’t access your bank account. The only information it knows about your finances and spending comes from receipts in your inbox or from your Wallet transaction history. I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.

SlideTag is a tiny digital photo frame that sits on a keychain, but it’s also a tracker compatible with both Apple’s Find My and Google’s Find Hub. You can load it up with photos and have the 6-color e-ink display cycle through at set intervals, or you can put something more practical on the screen.

The Kodak app makes it easy to generate a QR code, display a to-do list, countdown to a special event or just show you the current date in a nice calendar display. It’s incredibly easy to use, the color e-ink display is surprisingly good and setting up the tracking feature is super easy. This thing does exactly what it states it does, and with very little learning curve.

According to recent reports, so what’s the catch? You don’t really get to choose what the outside of your SlideTag looks like. These clever little photo frames are only available as a blind box, showcasing eight designs across the vibrant history of Kodak’s packaging and something Kodak calls a secret edition which is unique to this set.

In a recent development, I ordered two, and while both designs I found in the packaging are great there are other designs in the lineup I’d have chosen first. Some retailers are selling cases of eight SlideTags with promotional packaging like you’d see at the checkout counter of a grocery store, but this case does not guarantee you’re going to get all eight designs. There’s no real way to know what you’re going to get.

It has been revealed that that level of risk may not be your thing, but if you’re looking for a way to add a stealthy little tracker with no shortage of personality to your bag, backpack or purse I think this is a great option. It also makes a great little gift, perfect for a stocking or white elephant party. And if this level of cutesy fun isn’t your thing, Apple’s second generation AirTags are on sale for $18 this week.

Are Stablecoins a Threat to Visa and Mastercard?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (761 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Investors associate digital assets with extreme volatility.
  • In a recent development, but the industry also came up with stablecoins.
  • Visa (V -0.05%) and Mastercard (MA -0.18%) dominate the global payments landscape, each handling trillions of dollars in volume every single quarter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Neil Patel – Nov 25, 2026 at 9:21AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Visa ›.

Investors associate digital assets with extreme volatility. Look at Bitcoin's (BTC -1.43%) price chart, and this perception is warranted.

In a recent development, but the industry also came up with stablecoins. These are a type of cryptocurrency usually pegged to the U.S. dollar, and they're meant to hold their value. They leverage the speed and 24/7 runtime that blockchain networks are known for. This makes them particularly interesting in the world of payments where those traits matter tremendously.

Visa (V -0.05%) and Mastercard (MA -0.18%) dominate the global payments landscape, each handling trillions of dollars in volume every single quarter. Both companies haven't hesitated to promptly lean into the opportunities that stablecoins might offer. They're playing offense in an effort to protect their wide economic moats.

Still, there's certainly concern among shareholders that this technology could be a disruptive force. Are stablecoins a threat to the robust competitive positions of Visa and Mastercard?

In a Nov. 17 speech, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller remarked that "stablecoins are starting to be used behind the scenes to settle obligations among participants in card networks.".

Recent findings suggest that settlement is how the financial institutions on each side of a card purchase pay each other. Stablecoins are now part of that plumbing.

The stablecoin market was worth more than $300 billion earlier this month, according to research from The Motley Fool. That figure is up from $204 billion in January 2025. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in July 2025, established a federal rulebook for the U.S. stablecoins, adding a level of legitimacy to the industry.

Sources indicate that market cap isn't usage, though. McKinsey and Artemis Analytics estimate that reported stablecoin volume runs as high as $35 trillion a year, mostly from crypto trading and internal transfers. Real-world payments came to about $390 billion in 2025, just 0.02% of global payments. Business-to-business transactions, like paying overseas suppliers, made up $226 billion of that. Remittances and payouts are other practical uses.

Recent findings suggest that waller acknowledged that open blockchain networks "offer a upcoming paradigm for competition with traditional payment rails." Established players are responding by building their own blockchains, forming consortiums, or partnering with emerging crypto firms. But he also called traditional rails "a reliable backbone for final funds settlement." Stablecoins are being absorbed into the system. They aren't replacing it.

Recent findings suggest that visa and Mastercard are leading that response. Visa's stablecoin settlement run rate, which annualizes recent activity, surpassed $25 billion in the fiscal 2026 fourth quarter (ended Sept. 30), up 10x year over year. It now settles in five stablecoins across 10 blockchains and supports more than 225 stablecoin-linked card programs.

According to recent reports, mastercard made a purchase. It closed its acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure provider BVNK on Aug. 3, a deal worth up to $1.8 billion. It has since launched a platform that lets institutions manage fiat and stablecoin accounts side by side. In June, it announced stablecoin settlement for card issuers and acquirers, even on weekends and holidays.

Industry observers note that keep all of this in perspective. Visa handled $18.8 trillion in annualized payments volume in Q4. The stablecoin run rate equals roughly 0.1% of that pace. Stablecoins might provide an upgrade to how money moves between Visa's partners, but they aren't stealing volume.

In a recent development, the economic moats are about more than technology. Waller noted that established firms "have amassed customer relationships and associated network effects, along with the power of market confidence." A latest token doesn't come with Mastercard's 3.5 billion cards, merchant acceptance, or the fraud and dispute protections consumers trust.

And both companies have a long history of not shying away when new technologies emerge. They embraced e-commerce, mobile wallets, and tap-to-pay. Visa has issued more than 17.5 billion tokens, which replace card numbers with secure substitutes. Contactless now accounts for 81% of Mastercard's in-person purchase transactions.

A notable innovation to how money moves, stablecoins shouldn't be ignored by investors. However, they aren't a threat to Visa and Mastercard.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic latest look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP.

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a latest-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

Recent findings suggest that so far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a latest Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager stated. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

It has been revealed that “When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”.

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”.

By Daniel Foelber – Nov 25, 2026 at 9:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

It has been revealed that as of market close on Nov. 20, Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.11%) (BRKB +0.10%) is up 13.4% year to date, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.80%) is up just 1%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -1.54%) is clinging desperately to the green at 0.2% year to date, and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -4.27%) is down 2.7%.

The reversal is nothing short of jaw-dropping. Consider that, as of Sept. 30, Berkshire had a negative 0.9% year-to-date return while the Nasdaq was up 15.6%. Now, Berkshire is outperforming the major benchmarks by its widest margin since 2022.

Here's why investors are flocking to Berkshire amid market volatility and what history notes could happen next.

According to recent reports, warren Buffett. Image source: The Motley Fool.

After roughly six decades as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, Warren Buffett stepped down and passed the baton to Greg Abel on Jan. 1, 2026. Abel's capital allocation principles are closely aligned with Buffett’s. In his Feb. 28 letter to shareholders, Abel summed up those principles as follows:.

As CEO, Abel has eliminated or drastically reduced many of Berkshire's smaller positions and pole-vaulted Alphabet (GOOGL -5.32%)(GOOG -4.94%) from a new position in the third quarter of 2025 to Berkshire's fourth-largest holding behind Apple (AAPL -2.37%), American Express (AXP -1.37%), and Coca-Cola (KO +0.55%). However, he has also discussed his intention to maintain core sizable positions in Apple, American Express, Coca-Cola, and Moody's (MCO -1.10%) because these are companies that Berkshire understands well, has faith in their management teams, and expects to compound over the long term. In 2025, Berkshire collected a combined $1.668 billion in dividends from these four stocks, and their combined value closed the year at $158.617 billion. Berkshire's cost basis for the four positions combined is just $9.089 billion – a testament to the benefits of buying and holding quality businesses over an extended period.

NYSE · As of 11:12 AM ET 11/25/26.

Sources indicate that berkshire's steady approach can seem dull when the market is being driven higher by red-hot artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. But during times of intense volatility and crashing growth stock prices, Berkshire is a safe haven because of its disciplined capital allocation and fierce preservation of its reputation.

In 2022, the S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow all produced negative total returns (gains plus dividends reinvested), while Berkshire actually gained slightly on the year. Berkshire has posted double-digit returns every year since and is presently outperforming the major indexes by its widest margin since 2022. Over the last five years, Berkshire has exactly doubled as of market close on Nov. 20, easily outperforming the three major indexes. However, over the last decade, it is closer to in line with the S&P 500.

History reveals that Berkshire tends to have its greatest periods of outperformance when value stocks outperform growth stocks. Berkshire's public equity portfolio is chock-full of value stocks and dividend-growth stocks. Today, Apple resembles a modern-day consumer-staples giant more than a tech organization, especially given its steady cash flows and lower AI capital expenditures. Alphabet is ramping up AI spending, but it has historically generated very high free cash flow (FCF) thanks to steady ad revenue from Google Search and YouTube. Alphabet will likely return to positive FCF once it begins converting AI spending into profits.

Outside of its public equity portfolio, many of Berkshire's controlled businesses are steady cash cows. Berkshire generated $33.9 billion in net cash flows from operating activities in the first nine months of 2026. Its property and casualty insurance businesses, BNSF railroad, Berkshire Hathaway Energy, and ownership of several manufacturing, service, and retail businesses are worth far more combined than its public equity portfolio -- given that Berkshire's market cap is $1.21 trillion while its equity portfolio is worth $346.1 billion.

As of Sept. 30, Berkshire had a staggering $372.77 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments in U.S. Treasury bills (T-bills). This is especially appealing to value investors given interest rates on T-bills are at multiyear highs. With a cash reserve that's worth more than its entire stock portfolio, Berkshire has ample dry powder to buy excellent companies if their valuations become too cheap to ignore.

Sources indicate that there are timeless lessons in how Berkshire manages its operations and investment portfolio. Berkshire doesn't chase hot stocks or tether its performance to the benchmarks over the short term. Rather, it goes with its best ideas and lets compounding do most of the work.

Similarly, history indicates that buying Berkshire and holding it over the long term has proven to be an excellent investment. And there's every reason to believe that will continue under Abel. In fact, I could see Berkshire's returns improving if Abel casts a wider net and identifies more tech-focused companies, such as Alphabet, that have the potential to be excellent multidecade compounders.

Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1042 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • According to recent reports, high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • Industry observers note that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

According to recent reports, high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

Industry observers note that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

Sources indicate that spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

Sources indicate that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," mentioned Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he remarked.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone stated.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That noted, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

It has been revealed that "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, noted Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

Sources indicate that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

Sources indicate that the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, said Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he said. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

In addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she mentioned.

In a recent development, "It is isolated," she said. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she noted.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

According to recent reports, but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

It has been revealed that "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin mentioned. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

It's also important to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, said R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo stated.

Sources indicate that "That's when spreads really widen out," he mentioned. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

By Jennifer Saibil – Nov 25, 2026 at 9:45AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

Recent findings suggest that investors are finally becoming fearful. The market entered a correction last week, giving up all of its gains from this year, and it's now down almost 12% from its recent high.

It has been revealed that it's anyone's guess how much lower it will go and how long this will last. But if you pay attention to what famed investor Warren Buffett has always recommended, you can use these trends in your favor.

Recent findings suggest that one of Buffett's most well-known sayings describes his approach to investing. He cautions against trying to time the market, since it's not possible. Instead, he remarked, "We simply attempt to be fearful when others are greedy and to be greedy only when others are fearful.".

Greed is evident when the market becomes bloated, and that's measured in how expensive it is. Buffett developed his own metric for this, known today as the Buffett indicator.

In 2001, when the market had already begun to crash, he explained that the fall could be foreseen because the ratio of the total value of the stock market compared to the gross domestic product (GDP) was too high. He said that around 70% to 80% would be a value, and that 200% was "playing with fire.".

Recent findings suggest that he also correctly predicted that the crash at that time was far from over, and indeed, it lasted into 2003. While the market started climbing back up at that point, it didn't reach a upcoming high until 2007, right before the 2008 crash.

According to recent reports, today, the Buffett indicator is at 275%. That's down from nearly 300% as the market dips, and that's a good indication that this time, too, the correction may turn into a full crash. If it doesn't now, it will at some point.

Sources indicate that buffett is a value investor, and he aims to buy stocks that are undervalued relative to their intrinsic worth. The market isn't always rational, and it can misprice stocks for many reasons. Sometimes there's a short-term headwind that leads to a loss of confidence in an otherwise great tech giant that can bounce back, for example, and sometimes the entire market can go down, bringing top stocks with it.

According to recent reports, these are times when it can be scary for the average investor to plunge in. Ironically, while Buffett avoids risky stocks, he dives right into situations others would call risky. That's how he built up Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.11%)(BRKB +0.10%) into the formidable, market-beating stock it is today.

NYSE · As of 11:16 AM ET 11/25/26.

Consider what happened way back when Buffett first mentioned his famous words. He sensed a market crash coming when he wrote them in 1986, and the market lost more than 33% of its value in the 1987 crash. However, it gained 23% the next year.

That's when Buffett began to build Berkshire Hathaway's equity portfolio. In 1987, it owned only three stocks, in addition to its fully owned companies, and it picked up Coca-Cola in 1988, which remains its longest-held position.

Buffett credits a few great buys with his success, and when it's time to be greedy, you can also get your hands on potentially life-changing stocks.

United regularly use their own drones to film training sessions, but put up signs six years ago banning the use of them near the training ground in case they could reveal top-secret information to their opponents.

Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session has been leaked on YouTube.

Footage of the session was captured from a drone close to Carrington and uploaded online.

Man United players were captured during a drill under the gaze of Pochettino's coaching staff.

The footage was posted on YouTube by an account called CC Overview which insists that the airspace over Carrington is unrestricted and the drone was operating legally within Civil Aviation Authority rules.

It remarked that the video was taken half an hour into Pochettino’s training session and clearly shows the 54-year-old instructing the United squad along with his coaching team of No.2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya.

Perez, Jimenez and Sebastiano Pochettino have been at the training ground since the weekend after being given permission by the US Soccer Federation to leave after the first-leg against Haiti in Miami.

Pochettino addressed the Man United's internal media team for the first time on Thursday, outlining how he looks to drag this underperforming squad up the table.

'The culture is the most important,' Pochettino explained.

'Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

The breach comes as Man United prepare for a daunting trip to Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

The 12 minutes of drone footage captured Pochettino and his staff coaching across two training pitches at Carrington.

Man United installed signs in 2018 warning that the use of drones over Carrington was 'strictly prohibited' and would be reported for prosecution.

'We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us to be close to winning every single game.'.

'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Tuesday, a US jury convicted one of China’s key telecommunications and AI giants, Huawei Technologies, of stealing trade secrets from US tech firms and evading sanctions against Iran.
  • Although the longrunning charges stem back to 2018, the verdict coming now threatens to inflame US-China tensions at a sensitive time, just as Donald Trump prepares to increase tariffs on China.
  • The jury convicted Huawei of charges including bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the US, money laundering conspiracy, and “substantive” violations of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Tuesday, a US jury convicted one of China’s key telecommunications and AI giants, Huawei Technologies, of stealing trade secrets from US tech firms and evading sanctions against Iran.

Although the longrunning charges stem back to 2018, the verdict coming now threatens to inflame US-China tensions at a sensitive time, just as Donald Trump prepares to increase tariffs on China. In a press release, however, the US Department of Justice celebrated the outcome as critical to protecting the US financial system, the global telecommunications industry, and US national security.

The jury convicted Huawei of charges including bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the US, money laundering conspiracy, and “substantive” violations of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

According to recent reports, among crimes, Huawei was found guilty of “repeatedly” lying to banks about its business in Iran. Huawei also frequently lied to the US government that “it did not assist Iran’s government, military, or intelligence community,” the DOJ stated. In reality, the DOJ proved at trial that Huawei was conducting business in Iran under the name “Skycom” to evade sanctions, while providing Iran with “turnkey services with respect to an Internet backbone and broader accessibility for mobile networks.” Further, Huawei helped the Iranian regime “monitor and censor its owners’ access to the Internet” and provided surveillance cameras to monitor protests, the DOJ said. In a statement, the acting principal deputy assistant attorney general for national security, M. Scott Proctor, said Huawei “empowered our enemies” and “harmed our national security.”.

As the DOJ successfully argued, Huawei lied about its Iranian business specifically so that it could continue obtaining billions in US dollars by participating in a global marketplace that gave it necessary access to steal US tech. Among companies targeted, US Attorney for the Eastern District of Upcoming York Joseph Nocella Jr. stated that Huawei blatantly stole from T-Mobile and Cisco, as well as a semiconductor storage firm called CNEX and an antenna manufacturer called Quintel.

One of the stolen ideas was the design of a T-Mobile robot called “Tappy,” which helped the US firm “assess the responsiveness of touch screens by mimicking a human touch,” the DOJ said. To copy the design, Huawei signed a non-disclosure agreement, then sent photos and technical details back to China. Even bolder, when that intel was deemed insufficient, “a Huawei employee stole a part of the robot in his backpack and carried it out of T-Mobile’s controlled laboratory,” the DOJ said.

Huawei’s tactics weren’t always sophisticated, but they were effective, the DOJ noted, building into “a long-running conspiracy to steal intellectual property of US companies.” At trade highlights and tours of rivals’ facilities, Huawei employees would pretend to “get lost,” the DOJ said, so they could wander into restricted areas and take photos of hardware, The Latest York Times reported.

In a recent development, huawei engineers would also sometimes hide their activity by spelling words backwards. For example, Huawei was able to copy the source code used on Cisco routers—which the DOJ said was “identified as the ‘crown jewel’ of Cisco technology”—by taking notes in which they spelled Cisco as “ocsic.” Another time, the DOJ noted that a Huawei employee was caught “photographing proprietary Fujitsu equipment” while wearing a badge that falsely identified him as an employee of “Weihua.”.

During the trial, Meredith Arfa, a federal prosecutor, noted that Huawei employees were sometimes paid bonuses for their crimes, since the theft was so integral to Huawei’s business model, NYT reported.

Roman Rozhavsky, the assistant director of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division, said that Huawei spent years expanding its international enterprise “through theft of trade secrets, fraud, and other criminal conduct at the expense of US companies and the rule of law.”.

Recent findings suggest that huawei has been banned from selling its tech in the US since 2019, so NYT noted that the guilty verdict is unlikely to rattle the company’s finances much. However, the financial penalties stemming from the verdict could be steep, as the DOJ explained that they include “criminal fines, forfeiture, and restitution.”.

Sentencing is scheduled for September 14.

It has been revealed that huawei continues to deny any wrongdoing and rejects US claims that the Chinese Communist Party directed the thefts. NYT noted that Huawei’s investors have argued that the US fight is politically motivated and seeks to hobble “a Chinese initiative to build 5G networks around the world.”.

Outside the courthouse following the verdict, Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, told reporters that it’s significant that the jury did not convict Huawei of racketeering charges or conspiracy to obstruct justice. According to Heberlig, the examples of US technology theft merely represented “isolated misconduct by company employees,” which inevitably happens in a company so large, with “hundreds of thousands of people.”.

Heberlig confirmed that Huawei planned to appeal and considered the jury’s opposition to racketeering charges to be a “profound rejection of the United States’ narratives about what Huawei is.”.

“The allegations that the government made in this case overreached and simply weren’t consistent with the successful, innovative and hard-working company that we came to know and deeply respect in this trial,” Heberlig mentioned.

After the verdict, China “lashed out” at the US, AFP reported. According to Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun, the US is trying to use the ruling to “suppress” Huawei.

China “firmly opposes the US suppressing and containing Chinese enterprises and firmly supports Chinese enterprises in safeguarding their legitimate rights and interests,” Guo mentioned.

However, the FBI’s Rozhavsky suggested that even China, which frequently negotiates with Trump as the trade rivals continually clash, can’t spare Huawei from substantial penalties.

“This case serves as a stark reminder that the Chinese government continues to pose a serious threat to our economic and national security, but today’s guilty verdict proves the FBI and our partners will aggressively investigate, expose, and hold accountable those who target our nation,” Rozhavsky said. “No firm is too big, too powerful, or too well connected to exploit the US and its citizens and expect to escape American justice.”.

The Next Massive Healthcare Revolution Is Already Here. This Stock Could Cash In.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that blood tests used to happen because a doctor ordered one.
  • In a recent development, every one of those tests needs a lab, and for many of the biggest names in consumer health, that lab is Quest Diagnostics (DGX +0.10%).
  • According to recent reports, this isn't a someday story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt DiLallo – Nov 25, 2026 at 10:07AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Quest Diagnostics ›.

Industry observers note that blood tests used to happen because a doctor ordered one. Increasingly, people are ordering them for themselves. Function Health sells a membership that includes more than 160 lab tests a year for $365, and Apple is preparing to let iPhone owners order a panel of more than 50 biomarkers from its Health app for $119.

In a recent development, every one of those tests needs a lab, and for many of the biggest names in consumer health, that lab is Quest Diagnostics (DGX +0.10%). I think that makes it one of the better ways to invest in the shift toward proactive health.

According to recent reports, this isn't a someday story. Quest generated nearly $250 million in consumer revenue in 2025, including roughly $100 million from its own questhealth.com site, with the rest coming through partners such as Function Health and the wearables makers Oura and Whoop. Meanwhile, its Apple partnership rolls out later this year. Quest doesn't need to build the next hot wellness brand. It runs the labs and collection network behind several of them, so it gets paid whichever app wins the customer.

Quest's consumer revenue is growing briskly. Management said on its third-quarter call that consumer growth should top 30% this year. Growing 30% from $250 million implies roughly $325 million this year, which is about 2.7% of the $12.1 billion in revenue Quest expects at the midpoint of its guidance. That's small today, which is exactly why the runway matters.

NYSE · As of 11:13 AM ET 11/25/26.

Industry observers note that the consumer business isn't the only growth engine. Third-quarter revenue rose 10% to $3.1 billion, and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) climbed 15.4% to $3.00, driven by the strength of its physician, hospital, and consumer channels and productivity gains from automation and AI. Quest raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $11.25 to $11.35, a nearly 15% year-over-year increase. That's an acceleration from last year's 10% adjusted EPS growth rate.

In a recent development, the total U.S. and Canadian lab market is right now approaching $90 billion and is growing at a low-single-digit compound annual rate. Quest is growing faster, driven by acquisitions and other expansion initiatives, including new high-growth areas like consumer-initiated testing. It sees more than 20% compound annual growth potential from those new growth areas, much faster than the mid-single-digit growth rates of its legacy businesses.

If consumer-initiated testing became more mainstream, it could be a long-term growth accelerator for Quest and drive strong returns for investors. For example, if Quest delivered 12% annual EPS growth over the next decade, its EPS would reach $35 per share by 2036. Assuming Quest maintains its current valuation multiple of around 23x earnings, its stock would be worth over $800 per share a decade from now, a roughly 200% gain. Add in dividends (Quest yields around 1.3%), and the total return would be even higher.

Recent findings suggest that the bull case is below Quest's current outlook. The diagnostics firm expects to deliver 4% to 5% compound annual revenue growth and 7% to 9% compound annual EPS growth over the long term. If Quest's EPS grows 9% a year and the multiple eases to 20 times as growth matures, the stock reaches about $535 by 2036. That's a respectable but modest 7.5% a year. If growth slows to 6% and the multiple falls to 17 times, the stock reaches about $344, implying just 3% annual growth.

Industry observers note that several things could push Quest toward those outcomes. While consumer-initiated testing is a potentially high-growth area, there's no guarantee it will become more mainstream. Meanwhile, the continued upward pressure on healthcare costs could cause governments and insurers to push back against price increases, pressuring Quest's margins.

Sources indicate that quest doesn't have to invent the next breakthrough longevity platform. It can supply the testing behind many of them. For the bull case to play out, consumer-initiated testing needs to continue growing briskly, driven by strong uptake in partnerships such as its Apple Health panel. The early signs are positive, which makes Quest an exciting stock to hold for the next decade or more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

Industry observers note that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct concerns with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

Sources indicate that all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

In a recent development, joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

It has been revealed that “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca stated, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

In a recent development, momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Recent findings suggest that marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

In a recent development, marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

His team indicated an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

According to recent reports, they could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “newly introduced Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca noted “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Sources indicate that of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.
