📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.

It’s a big list. I check it twice (or 10 times).

By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.

According to recent reports, I should have plenty of opportunities this year. Nearly 2 in 5 holiday spenders (38%) proposal to use BNPL, according to NerdWallet’s holiday spending report. Concerningly, the same report found that a higher share of BNPL users expect they won’t be able to make their payments in full and on time compared to credit card users.

Using BNPL for holiday shopping isn’t inherently bad, but there are risks, including sneaky fees and the ease of loan stacking across many providers.

Here’s how to minimize those risks and set yourself up for success this holiday season.

Brenton Harrison, a certified financial planner in Nashville, notes many of his clients are turning to buy now, pay later in the “messy middle of life,” when everyday expenses are high and budgets are tight. This is especially true during the holidays.

In a recent development, “They have kids they're providing for, or they’re trying to go travel and see family,” Harrison says. “When those expenses pile up, it can be very attractive to be able to spread out payments.”.

Since BNPL divides your total purchase into smaller installments, typically due every two weeks, it feels easier on your cash flow than having to pay all at once.

In a recent development, while Harrison is open to his clients using BNPL, he emphasizes how important it is to understand the terms before opting in. BNPL apps only require a soft credit pull and a short application. When you can apply for a loan in just a few clicks, it’s easy to miss when payments are due or whether they’ll include interest.

But if clients understand the terms and are certain they can make the payments, Harrison claims BNPL's set repayment schedule can be a better option than more open-ended financing.

“With a credit card, [a holiday purchase] might be something that they buy over and over and over again, because that interest just continues to accrue over time, and they never pay it off,” he says.

Not all BNPL apps are created equal. I measure the top apps across multiple categories, but I weigh affordability the highest. My thinking is if you’re already strapped for cash, it’s a bad idea to pay extra just to break up the payments.

According to recent reports, there are providers, like Affirm and PayPal, that don’t charge interest with a common pay-in-four term (your total purchase, divided into four installments). They also charge no fees, including no late fees for missed payments.

Compare that to apps, like Sezzle and Zip, that may charge an automatic service or origination fee with your first installment, as well as late fees.

Long-term BNPL financing, which can stretch months or even years, usually includes interest, expressed as an annual percentage rate or APR. This is a more expensive payment option than a zero-interest pay-in-four.

Pay close attention to your checkout screen to see what you’re offered. Are the installment amounts equal or is the first installment higher than the others? That may mean there’s a fee. Do you see an APR listed? That means you’re paying interest.

Recent findings suggest that harrison points out that just because a store partners with a BNPL company doesn’t mean that’s your only option. Download a different BNPL app, search for the store and see if you get access to better terms, like a 0% offer.

Taking out multiple loans with different BNPL providers is known as “loan stacking,” and it’s risky.

Because you’re juggling different payment amounts due on different days, it’s hard to keep track of what’s coming out of your bank account. This is especially true if you set up automatic payments, which most BNPL apps require. If you overdraw your checking account, your bank will likely charge a fee.

According to research published in August by the Federal Reserve, 11% percent of BNPL consumers had a BNPL payment trigger an overdraft or nonsufficient funds fee from their bank in the prior year. People with less savings were even more likely to pay fees.

Before applying for multiple BNPL loans, look at a typical month of expenses and ask if there’s extra room in your budget for those payments, Harrison says.

“If you’re just assuming that because you’re spreading it out that you’ll be able to pay it, that's where I think people can get in trouble,” he says. “They set it and forget it, and they don't realize, ‘Oh, I am in no better position to pay that next month than I am this month, or I have three of these going at the same time, and collectively, it's more than I can manage.’”.

Most apps send payment reminders, so you can potentially reschedule the payment or change your payment method.

Industry observers note that still, it’s best to avoid the headache to begin with. If you’re feeling pressured to spend more this holiday season, communicate your limits clearly with loved ones, Harrison states, and avoid any loans you can’t comfortably repay.

“Think about the purchase itself, especially around the holidays,” he indicates. “There's a big difference between something that I can pay off over three months and something that I should have never been buying in the first place.”.

  • They also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two newly introduced credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

They also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

In a recent development, 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

Sources indicate that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for new applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

To maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

Travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

Recent findings suggest that the card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

With the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in Latest York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

Recent findings suggest that bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

However, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

According to recent reports, the earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

In a recent development, plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

Recent findings suggest that those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

One of the most interesting perks of the new cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

According to recent reports, there are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

  • Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a fresh manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 14:40 EST, 20 November 2026.

According to recent reports, diet Pep is losing his fizz. Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.

Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a fresh manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.

Three months in, and three defeats on the spin that left them six points behind Arsenal have made it clear that something is not clicking for Maresca.

Is the uncertainty around the potential punishment following that guilty verdict taking its toll? Is Maresca just suffering from his usual late autumn dips? He suffered similar tricky periods around late October and early November at Leicester and his first season at Chelsea too.

Or is there something at the heart of his side, of his system, that’s finally being exposed?

Enzo Maresca's Man City have slumped to three straight Premier League defeats after a promising start to the season.

Guardiola’s City was all about control. Keep the ball, dominate the pitch, play the game at your pace, on your terms.

Maresca’s City, regardless of how well they started the season, has been about anything but. It has been about triumph amid chaos, about moments of magic more than the overarching method.

Industry observers note that without that control, City’s defensive issues have been laid bare. The 13 goals they have let in after 10 games is their most at this stage since 2008. They haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last eight matches in all competitions. That's a drought longer than at any point under Guardiola.

Their biggest problem over City's three successive Premier League defeats is just how susceptible they have been to counter attacks.

Only Newcastle have faced more shots this season following ‘fast breaks’ – data giants Opta's term for counter attacks – than City’s 17, and 11 of those have come in the last three games: six against Nottingham Forest, two of which led to goals, three against Brighton and another two against Aston Villa.

In a recent development, maresca’s side are being more profligate in possession, too. Over the first seven games of the season, they lost the ball 120 times a game on average – one of the best figures in the division. Since then, it’s closer to 140.

City have been wasteful in possession and regularly overrun on the counter, with Elliot Anderson (centre) too often left isolated in midfield.

ANDERSON CAN'T DO IT ALL ON HIS OWN.

Many of these problems have their roots in Maresca's serious problems in midfield. Rodri, the best holding midfielder of his generation, was always going to be hard to replace but Maresca appears to be expecting Elliot Anderson to do it all on his own.

Anderson is at his best when he’s free to get up and down the pitch, box to box, using his physicality not just in winning the ball back but progressing it. No midfielder played more passes into the final third last season than Anderson at Forest. At one stage of the campaign, he had played more progressive passes than any other player across Europe’s top five leagues.

And yet Maresca is forcing Anderson to play as the sitter while his golden boy Enzo Fernandez, whom he pushed City to sign in the summer for £125million, is roaming free and high up the pitch.

Maresca likes his teams to build up in a 3-1-6 shape, which sees Fernandez push up as an extra attacking midfielder, and leaves Anderson manning the fort alone.

When City lose the ball, though, it leaves them wide open.

This is the opening goal City conceded against Forest. Josko Gvardiol wants to play the ball inside but has only red shirts and empty green space ahead of him. Anderson is the only man free, but even he is too high and has a Forest player ready to cut off the pass. Eventually, Gvardiol gets robbed and Forest score.

Industry observers note that A lack of options for Josko Gvardiol (left) led to Forest's opener against City. Enzo Fernandez (circled) was caught high up the pitch, way ahead of the deeper Anderson (also circled).

Here’s another moment in the defeat by Brighton.

According to recent reports, the Seagulls break forward on the flank and Anderson races over to close the ball down. Fernandez is, you guessed it, high up the pitch.

City have no midfield cover to stop the ball inside, Abdukodir Khusanov gets drawn in and leaves loads of space in behind for Yasin Ayari to exploit and cross to Maxim De Cuyper for a great chance.

The lack of protection offered by Anderson and especially the more advanced Fernandez was again on show against Brighton, who were able to exploit the acres of space left in midfield.

Industry observers note that fernandez is doing what Maresca wants, but it’s not working. Maresca needs more from him, especially when Anderson’s instincts are to press and harass and bully, which can leave gaps when he does not yet read the game as comprehensively as Rodri.

Sources indicate that anderson sits in the top five for ball recoveries among midfielders to have played 500 minutes this season. Fernandez is in the bottom five. That figure becomes even more alarming when you consider Anderson has created more chances from open play than Fernandez, too.

Recent findings suggest that ayyoub Bouaddi indicated at the World Cup that he had the most similar profile to Rodri. It might be time for Maresca to put some faith in him.

Recent findings suggest that maresca has always wanted his goalkeeper to be an 11th outfielder. In his one season at Leicester, Mads Hermansen played more passes than any goalkeeper in Championship history. During his time at Chelsea, there was a shaky moment in a draw with Arsenal when loud groans greeted a misplaced pass from Robert Sanchez.

‘I am the guy who asks Robert to do that,’ said Maresca after that game. ‘The moment he stops doing that, he is not going to play.’.

Donnarumma, though, for all his (usually) excellent shot-stopping, is anything but a ball-playing goalkeeper. The ball rolled under his foot from a simple back pass against Coventry and so nearly crept over the line. He gifted France an early lead while on international duty with Italy when he passed the ball straight to Michael Olise.

Only two keepers made more errors leading to shots than Donnarumma across the course of last season, with many of those being with his feet, like when he gifted Kai Havertz an equaliser in City's victory over Arsenal in April.

Gianluigi Donnarumma has never been good with his feet - now his excellent shot-stopping has taken a dip too.

The Italian should have easily dealt with Nicolas Jackson's second goal in City's 2-1 loss at Aston Villa.

The decision to let James Trafford leave in the summer, especially with Guardiola’s impending departure and a manager like Maresca coming in, is looking ever more misguided.

Trafford is not immune to mistakes either, of course. He erred badly when trying to play out from the back for City against Spurs last season and made an almost identical howler for Leeds at Bournemouth in October. But he is still far more confident at playing out from the back than Donnarumma.

The double blow for Maresca is that the trade-off with Donnarumma – where he makes up for his weakness with the ball at his feet by making saves that other keepers can’t make – is no longer paying off either.

Nicolas Jackson’s shot squirmed straight through him to hand Villa victory and condemn City to their first defeat of the season.

When you are coughing up chances as frequently as City are, Maresca needs his keeper to be on top form.

Do you know who is keeping the ball out of his net? James Trafford. He boasts the highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in the top flight, keeping out 81 per cent of the shots on target coming his way. Donnarumma is 15th, on less than 66 per cent.

According to Opta’s expected data, Trafford has also prevented more than four goals that he should have conceded from the quality of the shots he’s faced. Again, he’s the best in the Premier League. Donnarumma is middle of the pack.

Recent findings suggest that ‘At the moment, I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation,’ noted Maresca recently. Without Trafford there and just 34-year-old Geronimo Rulli as back-up, he doesn’t really have a choice but to persist with Donnarumma and hope he improves.

When the goals stop flowing for Erling Haaland, City can't mask all their other problems.

So used are we now to seeing the Norwegian on the scoresheet, having notched nine in City’s opening eight matches, that when he goes just two games without a goal it feels as if he’s on a barren spell.

The issue, though, is less down to Haaland and more that City’s build-up in recent weeks is struggling to get him into the game.

City are finding it more difficult to get Haaland on the ball. His touches per game are falling steadily but, crucially, so are the quality of the chances his team-mates are creating for him.

Haaland had more than one Opta-defined 'major chance' in five of City’s opening seven games. He’s had just one come his way in each of their three defeats.

His expected goals (xG) tally is dropping too. Across City’s winning streak, Haaland’s average xG per match was 0.81. Only once, against Liverpool, did it drop below 0.5.

Over the three defeats, it’s just 0.45 and has not once gone above 0.5.

Antoine Semenyo missing the last three games through injury has not helped, especially when teams now try to pack the middle of the pitch and force City wide.

Haaland will come good, he always does, but City need to start serving him again if Maresca wants to get through this tricky spell and stop the vultures from circling.

Latest Update: What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
  • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
  • An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

An interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any problems are documented.

Recent findings suggest that A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

Industry observers note that service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic concerns that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

Recent findings suggest that inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

Recent findings suggest that detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

In a recent development, reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

Industry observers note that the good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

However, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

It has been revealed that some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

Some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

Reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

It has been revealed that reddit consumers are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

Car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several owners suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The organization also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan.

According to recent reports, following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the tech giant's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the tech giant's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

Recent findings suggest that wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Industry observers note that social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

According to recent reports, specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active consumers in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

"Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," remarked the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently released Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the company's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

Next is semiconductor firm Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

According to recent reports, the five-star analyst mentioned that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the tech giant raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

Svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

In a recent development, operator: Thank you for standing by, and welcome to Autodesk's Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2027 Earnings Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] I would now like to hand the call over to Simon Mays-Smith, Vice President, Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

And now I will turn the call over to Andrew.

Andrew Anagnost: Thank you, Simon, and welcome, everyone, to the call. We delivered another strong quarter and signed our largest ever enterprise business agreement. Revenue and earnings per share were above the high end of our guidance ranges. Despite incremental headwinds from U.S. dollar appreciation, we've raised the midpoint of our full year billings and revenue outlook to reflect the third quarter beat and stronger underlying expectations for the remainder of the year. Autodesk strategy is to build project intelligence across the asset life cycle by connecting data, context and experience across design, make and operate. AI creates new opportunities to turn that accumulated intelligence into action, helping customers automate complex tasks, scale their expertise and deliver better outcomes.

Sources indicate that our work with a global engineering and consultancy company is an example of this strategy in action and shows how we are enabling our customers both to free up capacity to take on more work while also increasing human and agentic participation in our ecosystem. The company is collaborating with Autodesk to rethink how engineering work gets done, combining AI-powered workflow automation with access to decades of accumulated engineering knowledge. Together, we have developed an AI-orchestrated workflow in Revit that automates architectural documentation using model data and established drawing standards. In a focused test, the company reported a more than 90% reduction in drawing-generation time before accounting for full production review and quality assurance.

Even after those additional steps, it's estimated that net time savings could still reach at least 50%, alongside improved consistency and quality. This efficiency frees up capacity to do more and win more business. The potential extends beyond architecture. The company is exploring how similar capabilities could eventually support structural engineering, mechanical and electrical design, and other disciplines where documentation consumes significant time. The broader opportunity is to make specialized knowledge more accessible across the organization and improve engineering outcomes. The company has accumulated knowledge across thousands of projects, much of it embedded in models, documents and the experiences of its people.

It is exploring how Autodesk Assistant can make relevant insights into engineering workflows, helping engineers draw on past solutions, technical standards and calculations to make better decisions. AI can make the intelligence embedded in complex BIM models accessible to a much wider group of people, including those who aren't specialist modelers. This could broaden participation in project workflows and extend the value of that information and our tools across the organization. This collaboration also illustrates how our customer relationships are evolving. The tech giant increasingly sees Autodesk not simply as a software provider, but as a platform partner helping shape the future of engineering. It brings engineering expertise and real-world challenges.

Autodesk brings the technology and development capabilities to help solve them. This is the opportunity we see across our industries: moving beyond creating project information to turning it into reusable intelligence that expands what customers can accomplish. As knowledge from each project informs the next, it creates a reinforcing cycle of richer project intelligence, better decisions and more valuable outcomes across the asset life cycle. Janesh, over to you to discuss our quarterly financial performance and guidance.

Janesh Moorjani: Thanks, Andrew. We delivered another strong quarter in Q3, once again exceeding the high end of our revenue and EPS guidance. Overall, the underlying momentum of the business remained consistent with prior quarters, with continuing strength in AEC, particularly in construction and in emerging markets. Renewal rates remained strong, contributing to our outperformance in the quarter. The impact of our sales reorganization continued to diminish across most regions, with Western Europe remaining slower to normalize. Total revenue in the third quarter grew 17% as reported and 14% in constant currency. MaintainX had an outstanding first quarter within Autodesk, with revenue of almost $33 million and integration progressing as planned.

We plan to extend MaintainX across more geographies and segments next year, including through EBAs. We've already begun to build a good pipeline of opportunities. Please see the tables in our press release, earnings deck and Excel financials for details on our total revenue by product and region. Billings increased 12% as reported and 13% in constant currency, reflecting the underlying trends discussed earlier. We also closed several EBA renewals during the quarter as part of a sizable second half renewal cohort. RPO and current RPO growth continued to reflect the program to reduce multiyear discounts that we called out last quarter, including the wind down of multiyear renewals for the MaintainX-to-Subscription program.

Recent findings suggest that as we've said, we expect these dynamics will continue to weigh on total RPO and current RPO growth for some time. Turning to margins. Third quarter GAAP and non-GAAP operating margins were 26% and 39%, respectively. GAAP operating margin was broadly flat year-over-year, with underlying margin improvement and a further reduction in stock-based compensation as a percentage of revenue, mostly offset by the effects of the MaintainX acquisition. Non-GAAP operating margin was up approximately 1 percentage point. This primarily reflected operating leverage, the timing of investments and the benefits from our sales optimization, partly offset by margin dilution from the MaintainX acquisition. Third quarter free cash flow was $505 million, reflecting the timing of billings and collections during the quarter.

Industry observers note that moving on to capital allocation. We repurchased approximately 1.5 million shares during the quarter for $350 million. We now expect to buy back $1.5 billion of shares in fiscal '27, slightly ahead of our prior expectations and up from $1.4 billion last year. As I mentioned last quarter, we've made a few minor changes to simplify our revenue presentation and reflect the acquisition of MaintainX. We've summarized these changes in the slide deck on our website. Let me finish with guidance. Our guidance philosophy is unchanged.

In a recent development, our guidance continues to be based on the range of possible outcomes in our bottom-up sales forecast, which is grounded in the momentum of the business and embeds some prudence against our expectations of sales productivity normalization. We've continued to assume the macroeconomic environment will remain broadly stable through the remainder of the year. There are some incremental foreign exchange headwinds to billings from a stronger dollar. For billings, we've raised the midpoint of our fiscal '27 guidance range to $8.625 billion to reflect an underlying improvement in our expectations, partly offset by the additional headwinds from foreign exchange movements.

It has been revealed that as a reminder, our largest product subscription cohort and second largest EBA cohort in fiscal '26 create a tougher comparison this year, particularly in the fourth quarter. For revenue, we've raised the midpoint of our fiscal '27 guidance range to approximately $8.368 billion to reflect our strong results in the third quarter and an underlying improvement in our expectations, partly offset by a smaller tailwind from foreign exchange rates. As we outlined in February, our guidance still factors in a headwind to revenue growth from our sales reorganization earlier this year.

Industry observers note that while there is no longer any meaningful measurement benefit to billings or revenue from the Fresh Transaction Model, our full fiscal '27 revenue growth rate still has an approximately 1.5 percentage point tailwind from the first half of this year. For GAAP operating margin, we've increased our fiscal '27 guidance to approximately 27%, primarily to reflect an underlying improvement in our expectations. For non-GAAP operating margin, we've modestly raised our fiscal '27 guidance to a range of 39.2% to 39.3%, reflecting higher underlying margin from operating leverage. We continue to generate efficiency through the business while also investing more in our strategic priorities.

We expect fiscal '28 non-GAAP margins to improve modestly from our current guidance level despite the annualization of MaintainX operating costs. We remain on track to achieve 41% non-GAAP operating margin in fiscal '29. And for free cash flow, we've maintained our fiscal '27 range of $2.725 billion to $2.75 billion, reflecting strong underlying expectations, offset by the operating and net financing costs for MaintainX. We continue to manage our stock-based compensation with discipline. We expect stock-based compensation as a percentage of revenue to be about 9% in fiscal '27, which is within our targeted range and down from about 11% in fiscal '26.

In summary, we remain disciplined and focused on the controllable factors that drive our revenue, operating margin, earnings per share and capital allocation, which are the key building blocks of free cash flow per share. The slide deck on our website has modeling assumptions for the fourth quarter and full year fiscal '27. Andrew, back to you.

In a recent development, andrew Anagnost: Thank you, Janesh. Through our platform, industry clouds and AI, Autodesk is focused on creating project intelligence from connected design and making it accessible where customers work and make decisions. For our customers, this convergence increases efficiency and resilience, reduces risk and downtime and helps them deploy fewer resources to every project so they can bid on and win more projects with the resources they have. Let me give you some examples of our progress this quarter that demonstrate how this differentiated strategy works.

DPR Construction, a top 10 U.S. general contractor, renewed its enterprise agreement, building on a partnership of more than 15 years and continuing its use of Forma Build and Rhumbix to connect teams, partners and workflows from preconstruction through job site execution. Span Construction & Engineering, a U.S. steel building and design-build contractor, selected Forma for Construction to unify its project workflows and reduce system silos as it continues to grow. Foth, a U.S. engineering and consulting firm, standardized its infrastructure and environmental teams on Civil 3D and expanded its use of Forma as a company-wide design and project data solution.

In a recent development, in the U.K., a major regional water utility expanded its use of Forma to connect how it delivers capital projects with how it manages its water assets, carrying information created during construction into operations. In Southeast Asia, a diversified group adopted the Forma AECO Industry Cloud, initially piloting it with 1,000 people while expanding its use of Autodesk's AEC solutions to connect project documents, design data, owners, consultants and contractors across multiple business units as it advances its digital twin and AI initiatives. These stories have a common theme: creating project intelligence by converging people, processes and data across the project life cycle to increase efficiency and resilience, decrease risk and prepare for an agentic AI world.

In a recent development, this also strengthens Autodesk's growth potential, with construction sustaining strong growth and building on its momentum alongside our outstanding first quarter contribution from MaintainX. In manufacturing, customers are seeking convergence as they invest in their digital transformation to leverage granular and unified data and embrace the AI-driven automation capable of industry transformation. By consolidating on our platform, customers have the flexibility and connectivity across workflows to increase agility, innovation and resilience. Our customers are using more of Fusion's functional breadth, with larger installations and design through make convergence, which drove strong growth during the quarter.

Industry observers note that for example, in the U.S., John Zink, a global engineered solutions provider, selected Fusion, our cloud-based design, engineering and manufacturing platform, to replace a competitive solution as its global PLM platform, bringing more than 300 consumers into our Design and Make ecosystem and creating a foothold for broader PLM adoption across the enterprise. In Italy, engineering start-up Claret moved its industrial automation work to Fusion to give its distributed engineers cloud collaboration across design and manufacturing after a competitive design tool hit performance limits on complex assemblies. In India, a global engineering and product development company selected Fusion to expand from simulation into AI-assisted design with Autodesk Assistant and to spot manufacturing issues earlier and speed up design decisions.

And in Europe, a global industrial manufacturer extended its use of Flex, our consumption-based model, to give engineers across departments end-to-end access to our design, engineering and manufacturing tools, with the flexibility to bring in additional teams as needs evolve. As these examples show, customers are expanding their use of our platform, from global PLM deployments and cloud collaboration to AI-assisted design and flexible end-to-end access, bringing more teams into our Design and Make ecosystem. Let me finish by talking about AI. AI presents an extraordinary opportunity to expand the value software creates for customers. As with any major technology transition, it will reshape the competitive landscape, amplifying some existing advantages while creating new sources of differentiation.

We believe Autodesk is particularly well positioned to benefit from both. AI is fundamentally changing how software is delivered and consumed, accelerating the transition from stand-alone applications to specialized capabilities delivered on demand. As we discussed last quarter and reinforced at Autodesk University, our technology architecture brings together 3 key elements. Autodesk Assistant is the harness through which people can guide, review and apply trusted design and engineering capabilities. Autodesk Platform Services exposes the data models that deliver the industry context, workflows and project intelligence, while API and MCP interfaces make Autodesk capabilities available to applications and agents. And Autodesk's AI Orchestrator coordinates models, tools and capabilities to deliver accurate, fast and affordable outcomes.

Industry observers note that autodesk is making these capabilities available in 2 complementary ways: directly to agents within workflows where they can invoke trusted engineering services; and through Autodesk Assistant, where people can guide, review and act on AI-generated outcomes. This represents a fundamental shift in how customers interact with software. Rather than adapting their work to individual applications, customers can access the capabilities they need when and where they need them. Autodesk's advantage lies in bringing together decades of engineering expertise, industry-specific data and workflows, and the AI Orchestrator that is built on an open platform that can coordinate Autodesk capabilities alongside customers' and partners' own tools, data and AI models.

It has been revealed that together, these strengths extend the reach of our software while maintaining the precision, reliability and control our customers require. As AI models become more capable, inexpensive and interchangeable, differentiation increasingly depends on connecting them to proprietary capabilities to manage complex workflows with trusted data. Autodesk can combine probabilistic AI with deterministic engineering through the engines and intellectual property we own, delivering precise, reliable outcomes in the physical world while using AI to improve those capabilities. As the cost of intelligence falls, more workflows become economically viable to automate. We're already demonstrating how AI can orchestrate complex engineering workflows using trusted model data and established engineering standards, but the opportunity goes beyond productivity.

Industry observers note that it's about scaling expertise, making project intelligence accessible to more people, and enabling better decisions and outcomes across the asset life cycle. As more workflows flow through our platform, it creates richer project intelligence, improving the context for AI and the value of subsequent outcomes. This creates a reinforcing flywheel of greater automation, better decisions and more valuable capabilities. Richer project intelligence within our platform will not only amplify the value of our existing platform, but fundamentally expand what we can deliver, who we can serve and the value we can create for customers. Operator, we would now like to open the call up for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from the line of Saket Kalia of Barclays.

Saket Kalia: Andrew, maybe I'll start with you. And I want to pick up on your last comments there in your prepared sections. And maybe the question is, where do you stand on sort of the harness versus headless debate vis-a-vis Autodesk?

Andrew Anagnost: Yes, I don't really think that's much of a debate. We want to really meet our customers where they're at, but also recognize that they need more accuracy and precision and workflow orchestration than is possible with your frontier models today. So what we're doing is we're trying to be very agent-friendly. I mean, Fusion's a great example of this. You can see in the Fusion communities, a lot of people are using Claude and other types of tools to automate tasks in Fusion and drive various outcomes. And we love seeing that. We want to be where they're at, and it provides great exposure for our applications.

And they also have a strong need for precision in a lot of the work they do. So in our context layer, we capture who the user is, what they've done, their history, how they're working, where they're at in the design process. And then we orchestrate across various models, our models for higher precision and higher predictability and frontier models for the tasks the frontier models are good for.

So we're able to deliver speed, accuracy and cost effectiveness for our customers through the harness that we developed with the Autodesk Assistant. So we're meeting them in both worlds, headless for the agentic workflows, the Autodesk Assistant harness to deliver that speed, precision, that accuracy and that cost efficiency.

Saket Kalia: Makes sense, meeting the customer wherever they are. Janesh, maybe for you for my follow-up. Realize it's still early, but are there any high-level thoughts that you want to share on billings or revenue growth in fiscal '28 as we just think about fine-tuning our models?

Recent findings suggest that janesh Moorjani: Saket, I know a lot of people are thinking about that, although it's a bit early. But look, I'll start by saying the business is performing well. We've raised our full year guidance here to reflect our strong third quarter performance, as you've seen. We're seeing sustained demand across our industries, which now includes operations. Vruwink: Curious on your thought process around updating Fusion pricing and creating the 4 plan tiers as opposed to what has existed where accounts get to build out bespoke capabilities with the extensions. But partner compensation changes are just one part of the broader go-to-market model. All of the changes that we had were designed to put much more emphasis on new and expansion activity, and partners are adapting to those incentives. We rolled those incentives out for partners before we made the organizational changes ourselves on the Autodesk side. We also had to give them advanced notice before we rolled those changes out.

Sources indicate that the partners have been focused on this a little bit longer than some of the internal changes that we made recently. People are continuing to work diligently to drive upcoming business growth. We saw some of the initial productivity hits that we had expected at the start of the year, and we've seen many of those areas come back. Western Europe just continues to be the one area where we had rolled it out a little bit later because of the local laws and consultation requirements. According to recent reports, andrew Anagnost: Yes. The partners tend to lag a little bit off the internal team, but it's kind of a consistent pattern. They're all heading in the same direction, but the partners lagging a little bit relative to the internal teams.

According to recent reports, bhavin Shah: That's very helpful from both of you. Just a quick follow-up. Just as I'm thinking about the geo mix and the growth rates from the business, I think there's a little bit of a larger delta in terms of the Americas growth relative to EMEA and APAC this year than in prior quarters. Breaking: Digital Product Defaults Tech Companies Should Rethink

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1306 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that many users stick with the default settings of digital products, whether because they’re unaware of the alternatives or simply don’t take the time to explore them.
  • Below, members of Forbes Technology Council identify default settings and behaviors that tech companies should reconsider and explain why.
  • Calendar products should stop treating every free slot as usable time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that many users stick with the default settings of digital products, whether because they’re unaware of the alternatives or simply don’t take the time to explore them. That means seemingly minor product design decisions can have an outsized impact on users’ privacy, security and everyday productivity.

Below, members of Forbes Technology Council identify default settings and behaviors that tech companies should reconsider and explain why. They also share how more thoughtful choices on the part of product developers could build trust, reduce risk and improve the user experience.

Calendar products should stop treating every free slot as usable time. If the default availability exposes the whole day without setup, travel or recovery buffers, colleagues book meetings back-to-back, and the owner must absorb the collision. Few users know to configure hidden buffers, so the schedule rewards whoever books first. Build a small, visible transition gap into availability and let people shorten it when their work allows. Show clear buffers beside each slot. - Jagadish Gokavarapu, Wissen Infotech.

Tech companies should rethink enabling AI-generated recommendations or automated actions by default. Users may not realize when a system moves from assisting to acting on their behalf. Products should make that distinction clear, keep consequential actions subject to explicit approval, and allow users to change those permissions easily. - Vibhor Kumar, EDB Postgres AI.

In a recent development, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

Apps should not request access to contacts, location, microphones or photos before those capabilities are actually needed. Just-in-time permissions give users better context for their decisions and reduce unnecessary exposure of personal data. Convenience should not require unrestricted access. - Prashanthi Kolluru, KloudPortal Technology Solutions Pvt Ltd.

In a recent development, business software should distinguish an unanswered field from a confirmed zero. In a sales forecast, zero should mean no revenue is expected, not that nobody entered an estimate. Consumers often leave prefilled values untouched, making incomplete forecasts look finished. Default to “not provided” so managers can see where information is missing before relying on the totals. - Nicholas Domnisch, EE Solutions.

Two-factor authentication is crucial. There are still far too many companies that don’t require any other form of authentication besides username and password. Enabling two-factor authentication is one of the best ways to protect yourself from phishing and compromised credentials. I urge every company to consider shipping their product with two-factor authentication turned on. - Mark Beare, Malwarebytes.

Recent findings suggest that tech companies should rethink enabling AI features by default without making data use clear. A user accepting convenience is not necessarily consenting to their data being retained or reused. Default to minimum data collection, explain the trade-off and let users choose. Responsible AI starts with the decisions we make on users’ behalf. - Helen Wang, Apex Group.

Recent findings suggest that few users change defaults, so the default sets how much oversight most people get. AI features that act on their own are a good place to rethink it. For consequential actions like a cash withdrawal or a self-checkout override, start with a quick human confirmation. Once evaluations show the AI handles edge cases reliably, loosen that step and let users choose. - Andy Zosel, Diebold Nixdorf.

Recent findings suggest that I’d rethink the default sorting in business software. For example, when CRM people see records ordered by recent activity rather than what needs attention, urgent opportunities can disappear beneath less important updates. Defaults should prioritize the next useful action, not simply what changed last. That small design choice can shape decisions across an entire team. - Sergii Grushai, Peeklogic.

It has been revealed that notification settings need to be rethought. Most products ship with everything on, and most consumers never touch the setting, so the default becomes the policy. People then mute the whole channel and miss the one alert that mattered. Default to tiered, role-based alerts where only critical items interrupt and the rest roll into a digest. In operations, the alert nobody reads is worse than no alerts at all. - Steven Singer, Arbill.

Asking for location access only once, at setup, is something to rethink. People tap “Yes” to get started, and the app keeps collecting data in the background for years afterward. The company ends up holding a movement history that it never needed for every customer and that it now has to protect. Ask for location access at the moment a feature needs the user’s location and for that session only. - Kriti Faujdar, Yelp.

Privacy settings should prioritize user protection rather than maximizing data collection. Users shouldn’t need to navigate complex settings to safeguard their personal information. This means companies need to build privacy into products by design, clearly explaining how data is used and ensuring broader sharing is always an informed choice. - Anastasia Georgievskaya, Haut.AI.

Audit logging is a setting that’s often overlooked. Many SaaS platforms ship with minimal logging or keep logs for only days, with the detailed tier sold as an upgrade. Often, no one really notices until an incident happens, and then the evidence is simply gone. Default to logging that actually supports an investigation; you can’t reconstruct what you never recorded. Review your logging and how you audit the logging process. - Dan Sorensen, Nexus Security Advisors.

One that I would question is the default implementation of all newly introduced features for current users. A feature that might seem great to a product team may end up disrupting the workflow that a user has learned over many years. Users do not change defaults until there is a problem. Companies should implement new features gradually, with explanations of why the change is good and how to go back. - Ajay Pandey.

Recent findings suggest that training AI on customer content needs to be rethought. Several platforms now feed what people post into their models unless the user finds an opt-out, and most never will. When nearly everyone leaves a default in place, the default is the manufacturer’s choice, not the customer’s consent. I would make model training opt-in, explain the trade in plain language at the moment it matters, and accept a smaller dataset. - Brandon Fuchs, Balenor Pharmaceuticals Inc.

In a recent development, data sharing set to “on by default” needs to be reconsidered. Most people never open privacy settings, so whatever ships enabled becomes their consent in practice. In health apps and connected devices, that can mean sensitive information flowing to advertisers or partners without real awareness. Making data sharing opt-in protects trust, reduces regulatory risk and treats patients as decision makers. - Will Conaway, Tuxedo Cat Consulting.

Sources indicate that single sign-on should be made the default option. Not only does it free up the end user’s mental capacity, but it also gives the IT department tighter control over the software. Yet, if it isn’t implemented during the initial rollout, it is seldom added later. - Kevin Korte, Univention.

The “Remember this device” setting should grant temporary rather than indefinite trust. A laptop can be known by a product long after it is no longer owned or used exclusively. Let device trust be time-limited and easily inspectable. Device recognition does not imply the same person now owns the laptop. - Kavitha Thiyagarajan, Newrez LLC.

For years, companies have defended their brands against online fraud by registering a huge defensive domain portfolio and setting them to auto-renew. But changes to the internet and the nature of business have made this unsustainable. A robust defensive portfolio now needs to cover tens of thousands of domains, or more. The cost, effort and risks have skyrocketed. Truly proactive protection, such as domain blocking, is now a crucial tool in the brand protection toolkit. - Tony Kirsch, Brand Safety Alliance (a GoDaddy Registry Initiative).

What Are Repositioning Cruises?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1049 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
  • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
  • Recent findings suggest that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

Recent findings suggest that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

Recent findings suggest that one key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

Sources indicate that another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

Recent findings suggest that just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a latest region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit important sites when off the ship.

Sources indicate that if there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

For ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy demonstrates, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

Recent findings suggest that many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

In a recent development, if you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

You can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

It has been revealed that here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

This journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between Newly introduced York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

Sources indicate that departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

If Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and Fresh England before reaching the Significant Apple.

Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching New York.

#120391. Industry News: The Model Is Only Part Of The Story: Why Enterprise AI Needs A Control Plane

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1045 w)

Industry News: The Model Is Only Part Of The Story: Why Enterprise AI Needs A Control Plane

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1045 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kameshwar Singh is a Director of Engineering at Cohesity focused on Enterprise AI, Agentic AI, AI governance, automation, and responsible AI.
  • Nearly every enterprise AI discussion I sit in begins with the same question: Which model should we standardize on?
  • Industry observers note that scale makes these questions pressing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kameshwar Singh is a Director of Engineering at Cohesity focused on Enterprise AI, Agentic AI, AI governance, automation, and responsible AI.

Nearly every enterprise AI discussion I sit in begins with the same question: Which model should we standardize on? Fair, but no longer the most important one. As AI moves from pilots into co-pilots, production applications and agents that act on their own, leaders need harder answers. Which AI systems are running in our environment, who or what is calling them, what can they reach and do, and how fast can we pull the plug?

Industry observers note that scale makes these questions pressing. Gartner projects that a typical large global enterprise will be running more than 150,000 agents by 2028, up from fewer than 15 in 2025, yet only 13% of organizations are confident their agent governance is adequate.

Enterprise AI needs a control plane: not another product on the shortlist, but an architectural layer providing visibility, enforceable policy and the ability to intervene across everything AI touches.

Each agent should carry its own identity, defined permissions, a named human owner and a documented purpose. That sounds elementary, yet CyberArk’s 2025 State of Machine Identity Security Report counts 82 machine identities for every person, and most identity programs were built for human employees.

Recent findings suggest that I came up through Unix, and I think about agents the way I think about a shell: You do not need hundreds of commands when one capable interface can run nearly anything beneath it. An agent with one open-ended “execute script” tool may pose far more risk than one with 50 tightly scoped tools.

Sources indicate that so the useful question is not which tools an agent may call, but what this identity can ultimately do, against which resources, under what conditions. Least privilege, time-limited access and approvals should bind to the identity, not to a tool catalog.

AI workloads do not all carry the same risk, so they should not all be routed the same way. Policy sets the boundaries first: Data sensitivity, jurisdiction and risk tolerance decide which models are even eligible. Capability comes next: Among the eligible models, which one can actually do the job? Cost and latency settle the choice last.

A workload touching regulated customer data may belong on a privately hosted model; a sovereignty-sensitive one may require an approved regional environment. Routine summarization can run on a smaller open-weight model, while a hard reasoning problem may still deserve a frontier model. The strongest model is rarely required; the cheapest is not automatically right.

Industry observers note that the FinOps Foundation’s State of FinOps 2026 report found that 98% of FinOps teams expect to be managing AI spend within the year, up from 31% two years earlier. Token consumption belongs in the same telemetry as security events, because a spend spike is often the first sign an agent has gone off script.

In a recent development, the model is one component among many. The moment an agent can retrieve sensitive information through an API or invoke powerful actions through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, those interfaces become part of the AI control boundary. IBM’s 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that more than 20% of organizations reported a breach involving AI models or applications, and the most frequent causes were compromised APIs, applications and plug-ins around the model rather than the model itself.

Recent findings suggest that I picture the full chain of an interaction: identity, application, agent, model, data, tool and action. Visibility must cover every link, because attackers target the unwatched one. OWASP’s Top 10 for Agentic Applications makes the same case from the offensive side, listing goal hijacking, tool misuse and privilege abuse. The control plane should span that whole chain, with a loop from the final action back to the originating identity so any link can be revoked, blocked or isolated.

It has been revealed that when an agent begins reading datasets it has never touched, extracting far more records than usual or running up abnormal costs, an alert is not enough. You need the ability to respond: revoke credentials, terminate the session, block the tool or isolate the workload. Ask your security team whether they could shut down one misbehaving agent within minutes without disrupting the application around it.

According to recent reports, gartner expects that by 2027, 40% of enterprises will demote or decommission autonomous agents because governance gaps surfaced only after a production incident. Controls should scale with autonomy and risk, not one rulebook for all.

In the reference architecture I have been developing, the control plane comprises seven capabilities: inventory and ownership; identity and access; data and knowledge governance; model policy and routing; API, MCP and tool governance; observability and FinOps; and threat detection and response.

The structure should also remain open. AI is moving too fast to anchor an enterprise to one model, platform or vendor. Products will come and go; the architecture should not have to. Every component ought to be replaceable, which means open standards and loose coupling.

According to recent reports, the hardest design decision is what to centralize. My answer: Centralize the inventory, policy definitions and audit trail, because each needs a single source of truth, and keep enforcement distributed across the identity, security, data and application platforms you already run, because that is where controls execute. Governance is an operating model, not a product.

For CIOs, CISOs and CTOs, here are four steps to follow for the coming quarter:.

It has been revealed that 1. Inventory every AI application, agent, model, MCP server and API in use, and attach a named owner to each.

2. Assign every agent a unique identity and review what it can ultimately do, not merely which tools it lists.

3. Write a routing policy that decides in order of policy, capability and cost.

4. Rehearse containment: Revoke, terminate and isolate a test agent, and record how long it takes.

The organizations that scale AI safely will not be the ones with the best model, but the ones with the best architecture around it.​.

It has been revealed that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?
