Industry observers note that five days ago, if you recall, a report from TrendForce sparked a sell-off in Micron stock. According to TrendForce, Chinese companies were cutting back on memory purchases, causing NAND spot prices to fall 20%.

And so Micron stock started falling.

Five days later, Micron's still falling as TrendForce publishes a fresh report: "Chinese [cloud service providers] have reduced their 2027 memory orders." And more NAND supply is coming to market, creating an "oversupplied market" and "a downward pricing cycle" in NAND.

NASDAQ · As of 11:16 AM ET 11/25/26.

The better news is that the reason NAND sales are down appears to be that Chinese companies can't right now get all the GPUs they want, such that they need less NAND to pair with GPUs. This implies that if China does get access to more GPUs in the future, the NAND situation may fix itself.

But the best news of all is the situation with DRAM:.

Recent findings suggest that although prices may "moderate," TrendForce states the DRAM market "is expected to remain undersupplied" in 2027. When Chinese buyers cut DRAM orders, the supply is "promptly absorbed" by American buyers. As a result, TrendForce expects DRAM supply to remain tight in 2027 -- and total DRAM sales could grow 69%!

I don't know about you, but to me, that still sounds incredibly bullish for Micron stock.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it’s cold outside, it’s the ideal time to stay home, organize your finances, set some newly introduced money goals and make progress toward them.

That’s the promise of the viral winter money trend known as “The Great Lock In” that’s circulating on social media.

Sources indicate that “You’re probably not doing too much,” notes Robert Baird, wealth manager at Cornerstone Financial Services in Southfield, Michigan. “It gets dark early. So those can be great months to lock into saving and not spend in excess.”.

One important component of the Great Lock In is developing upcoming routines that will last well into 2027, notes Jordan Mangaliman, founder and fiduciary wealth advisor at GoldLine Wealth Management in Fullerton, California.

“We want a long-term habit versus a Band-Aid fix,” he says. “In today’s economy, money goes in and out so blindingly fast.”.

Ready to join the movement? Here’s how to get started.

What’s your money moonshot? Maybe it’s paying off all your credit card debt or purchasing a home. Or spending less than you earn. Defining it is the first step toward achieving it.

“Spend a lot of time identifying what that goal is,” Baird says. “Everyone’s in a different position, so comparing yourself to what you see online might not be applicable.”.

Even while setting ambitious money goals, it’s worth grounding them in reality, Mangaliman says.

If you want to save a larger portion of your income, he suggests trying the new saving pattern for a couple of months to see how it feels rather than saying you’ll do it forever and then getting frustrated.

“It’s a marathon, not a sprint,” Mangaliman adds.

Once you’ve outlined those big goals for your Great Lock In, create a budget to help you achieve them, Baird states.

Sources indicate that he suggests combing through your previous credit or debit card spending to see where your money is going. Then you can decide what you want to change or shift. Using a tool like the 50/30/20 budget calculator can also help. This approach allots 50% of take-home pay toward needs, 30% toward wants and 20% toward savings and debt payments beyond the minimum.

Baird suggests including saving as a line item in your budget so you don’t forget to do it. “Building that cost into your budget will put you in a better position later,” he says.

Any Great Lock In should include growing your savings, because that makes achieving other goals easier, Baird indicates.

In a recent development, “Maybe there’s something you could cut in the short term to build up that savings,” he claims. Good targets include subscription services, food delivery, entertainment and travel costs.

Saving more is especially challenging in today’s environment, when everyday expenses like gas are higher than they were a year ago.

Baird indicates that makes winter a good time to try to reduce costs. There can be fewer temptations to go out and spend money when the days are shorter and the temperatures are colder.

Mangaliman recommends setting aside three to six months’ worth of expenses, although even a smaller amount is helpful. “Ultimately it’s about what you can afford,” he notes. “It’s the foundation of your financial house.”.

Along with building savings, paying down high-interest debt is another pillar of the Great Lock In.

With credit card interest rates higher than they were a few years ago, carrying credit card debt has gotten more expensive. “I would consider applying some savings to paying down debt, especially right now when your debt is costing you more than you can earn in savings,” Baird says. (You still want to reserve an emergency fund to cover unexpected expenses.).

According to recent reports, “High-interest debt is one of the biggest thieves of wealth,” Mangaliman says. And one way to avoid turning to debt again in the future is to build up that emergency fund so it’s there for you if you need it.

Even when you are committed to a Great Lock In, some hiccups along the way are inevitable. Success depends on continuing anyway.

“It’s like a diet,” Baird claims. “Just because you ate ice cream on a Sunday doesn’t mean on Monday you can’t go right back to being disciplined again.”.

“Be kind to yourself and do everything in moderation,” Mangaliman suggests. Just wanting to improve your finances is already a great first step, he indicates.

It has been revealed that in fact, he embraces the Great Lock In mentality himself. “There’s an old saying: It’s not how you start, but how you finish,” he says. “And you want to finish the year on a strong note so you carry those habits into 2027 and beyond.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lindsey Witmer Collins is Founder and CEO of WLCM.AI, an Inc. 5000 manufacturer building AI solutions for enterprises, and Scribbly Books.

In a recent development, ​I know how that sounds, and I know it makes me seem uninformed or naive, but I’m really just trying to make an important choice thoughtfully. It’s a choice we all get to make: How do I orient myself to the world I’m in and the one I’m building? And, specifically, I’m curious. What if we ran our projections for the future of humanity in the opposite direction than the doom default? In other words, what if the future is awesome?

Our feeds show many flavors of doom: AI is coming for the jobs, the planet is cooking, the kids can’t look up from their phones and somewhere a robot is learning to do backflips. I build software for a living, including the kind people are nervous about, so I’m not saying this from a hammock. I’m looking for evidence.

A good place to understand where we’re going is to see where we’ve been—to understand what we care about, what we’re capable of and what direction, as a species, we trend toward.

If you were born in 1800, there was, globally, roughly a 43% chance you’d die before your fifth birthday. Today, it’s about 4%, and in most of the world it’s lower than that. Nearly 80% of humanity lived in extreme poverty two centuries ago; by 2019 it was under 10%, and since 1990 the count has dropped by something like 130,000 people every single day. In 1820, 1 adult in 10 could read. We’re at 87% now.

According to recent reports, none of that happened by accident. It happened because somebody figured out that germs exist, that a cowpox sore could stop smallpox, that nitrogen could be pulled out of thin air and turned into fertilizer. Somebody built the sewer. Somebody built the washing machine—Hans Rosling used to call it the greatest invention of the industrial revolution, and his argument was basically that it gave his mother back enough hours to read to him.

In a recent development, my great-grandmother could walk into my kitchen today—hot water out of a wall, a box that keeps food cold, a cabinet of medicine that works, the whole of recorded human knowledge in the pocket of my jeans—and conclude she had died and gone to heaven. To me it’s just Monday, and I’m a little annoyed about the traffic.

The pace never slowed down; the headlines just moved on to other things. The International Energy Agency called solar the cheapest electricity in history back in 2020, and it has kept getting cheaper. Lithium-ion battery packs ended 2025 averaging $108 per kilowatt-hour, down 93% since 2010, which is the reason the grid, my electric car and the battery in my lawnmower are all getting electrified without a modicum of drama.

Industry observers note that in December 2023, the FDA approved the first CRISPR-based therapy, for people with sickle cell disease—a disease we’ve understood at the molecular level for decades and could do very little about until now. Twenty-five African countries now give malaria vaccines as part of routine childhood shots, and they’re more than 39 million doses in. This year, four astronauts flew around the moon for the first time since 1972, and an mRNA flu shot got approved after beating the traditional one by about 27% in a trial of nearly 50,000 people.

According to recent reports, and AI—which we love to fret about—is mostly busy doing the routable work: the reading, the sorting, the first draft, the thousand small lookups. That raises the value of everything it can’t reach, and most of what it can’t reach is other people.

I spend most of my time now on an above-ground mining startup focused on the critical minerals and materials sitting in the U.S.’s retiring infrastructure—EV batteries, solar panels, telecom copper wires and so forth. A surprising share of the next decade’s supply is already here, waiting to be recovered, and it’s on the verge of happening.

What if we get all of the benefits of technology, and we still love each other, and hang out, and chat with the person at the checkout?

Picture a backyard cookout in 2075. Grandma is 120 and bringing her famous potato salad, because the cataract fix was an afternoon, her hip came out of a printer and she’s been weightlifting her entire adult life. The power for the whole event—the grill, the speaker, the car that drove her over—cost roughly nothing, because sunlight is free and we finally got good at storing it. The toddler running laps around the table will learn of malaria only in history books. Somebody’s cousin runs a three-person manufacturer that would have needed 40 people in 2020. And we’re still watching live sports in the living room.

If the lines on the charts to keep going the way they’ve gone for 200 years, and if we keep showing up with a side dish, we might end up better than fine.

It has been revealed that we’re all makers and builders in our own unique ways, and we build what we see in our mind’s eye. If the only future we picture is the grim one, we might start driving off the road.

In a recent development, I’m going to say we’re building a beautiful and abundant future, and that things will keep getting better. You may say I’m choosing my facts selectively, and you would be correct. There are too many facts, so we all get our pick.

It has been revealed that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

It has been revealed that “I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”.

They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

“We feel ready,” Alonso mentioned. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”.

Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”.

These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Stefon Walters – Nov 25, 2026 at 10:45AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.

In a recent development, I've always been a fan of ETFs because they make investing straightforward and check many boxes at once. They don't usually get the same attention as individual stocks because they aren't as flashy, but they can be just as rewarding.

As we get close to 2027, it's a good time to see how ETFs can fit in your portfolio. Personally, there are three I'm loading up on. Two are staples I routinely invest in, and one will be a new addition. We can't predict how the market will move, but in the event of a market crash, they're investments I expect to bounce back and thrive over the long run.

I routinely invest in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -2.90%) because it essentially invests in the U.S. economy. The 500 companies in the S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.80%) account for much of U.S. economic activity, so they typically move in the same direction over time. The stock market is notoriously irrational, so sometimes there's a short-term disconnect between the two, but they tend to move hand in hand over the long haul.

Recent findings suggest that if there's an investment I wouldn't think twice about holding through a market crash, it's VOO. The S&P 500 has experienced its fair share of market crashes, surviving and thriving after each one.

NYSEMKT · As of 11:16 AM ET 11/25/26.

In a recent development, past results don't guarantee future performance, so we don't want to assume it will always happen, but the S&P 500 is built to grow over time. Its composition changes over time as companies rise and fall, but overall, the index rewards winners.

Right now, big tech is leading the way (and that'll be the case for a while), so much of VOO's performance depends on a handful of stocks. This isn't quite ideal from a diversification perspective -- and largely why it's down 4.8% in the past month (as of Nov. 23) -- but it has been working in the index's favor over the past few years.

In a recent development, you can't control or predict how a stock price will move, but you can count on a reliable dividend. Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD -0.07%) provides that. It's known for holding high-quality companies because it requires companies to have at least 10 consecutive years of dividend payments, five consecutive years of dividend increases, and be in good financial health.

NYSEMKT · As of 11:16 AM ET 11/25/26.

If a market crash happens, it's good to have dividends coming in, no doubt, but it's even better when they come from businesses that have stood the test of time and offer strong stability. Take its top holding, Procter & Gamble, for example. P&G isn't a sexy, high-flying tech company, but it sells products that people buy regardless of market or economic conditions. It's also a Dividend King, or a company that has raised its payout for 50 years or more, with 70 consecutive years of dividend increases.

Even with this year's impressive run-up, SCHD maintains an attractive yield. The stock is up 25% this year, so its yield is lower than usual, but at 3.1%, it's still good for a 102-stock ETF.

SCHD Dividend Yield data by YCharts.

In a recent development, I don't at the moment own shares of the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX -7.67%), so adding it to the portfolio heading into 2027 is a matter of buying the dip. It has been on a downtrend since its June 22 high.

NASDAQ · As of 11:13 AM ET 11/25/26.

SOXX holds 30 semiconductor (chip) stocks, ranging from manufacturers to designers to equipment makers. The current AI boom has brought chips to the spotlight because they're crucial for training and developing AI models, but they've been the backbone of the electronics we use for many years.

There's overlap between SOXX and VOO with big tech names like Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Intel, and Nvidia (SOXX's top five holdings), but they make up a higher concentration in SOXX, allowing you to take advantage of the industry's upside without picking a "winner.".

In a recent development, semiconductor companies are for sure on a high with the current AI boom, but regardless of how it plays out, the need for semiconductors will only keep growing. I like the industry's direction.

Latest Update: The AI Infrastructure Bet That Smart Enterprises Are Making

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (904 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Paul Deraval, Cofounder & CEO of NinjaCat, is a software veteran with 20+ years driving innovation in martech, AI and agency growth.
  • According to recent reports, right now, companies of all sizes and sectors are racing to adopt artificial intelligence.
  • For many enterprises, this means increasing access to AI tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paul Deraval, Cofounder & CEO of NinjaCat, is a software veteran with 20+ years driving innovation in martech, AI and agency growth.

According to recent reports, right now, companies of all sizes and sectors are racing to adopt artificial intelligence. Many consider AI the next major thing, and no one wants to miss out.

For many enterprises, this means increasing access to AI tools. They are paying for Claude subscriptions, licensing ChatGPT Enterprise and rolling out Microsoft Copilot across departments. According to Gallup’s latest workplace survey, 47% of employees say their organization integrated AI tools in Q2 2026, up from 41% the previous quarter.

Unfortunately, more tools don’t necessarily equate to better outcomes or higher productivity, and many executives aren’t seeing ROI even as they spend millions on software seats and infrastructure. A National Bureau of Economic Research study found that 89% of executives reported AI had “no impact on labor productivity.” ​.

Companies have real reasons to be excited about AI, but those that use it to gain a competitive advantage and add real value will invest in the governance and infrastructure needed to operationalize these models effectively at scale. As Forbes contributor Güney Yıldız reports: “AI spend does not become ROI simply because usage goes up. Value capture requires workflow redesign, not just license distribution.”​.

Here’s how forward-thinking leaders can redesign workflows to achieve real ROI from their AI investments.

Sources indicate that AI should deliver tangible outcomes like making work easier, better or cheaper. Its purpose is not, as many leaders mistakenly assume, to simply increase AI adoption or add another tool to the technology stack.​.

According to recent reports, executives can be forgiven for misunderstanding that point. Adoption can feel like action, and they face immense pressure to act. In reality, enterprises have different teams, roles and workflows, each with its own needs. Some can benefit from an AI tool or autonomous agent while others really don’t.

Rather than forcing an AI tool or agentic layer into every process, match AI capabilities to a specific problem. Right now, many businesses conflate success with usage. However, as the tokenmaxxing debacle indicates, measuring usage isn’t the same as promoting real impact.

Instead of just measuring AI use, audit workflow bottlenecks before selecting tools so their capabilities match the problem they’re trying to solve. At the same time, prioritize tools that embed directly into existing systems, so workflows stay integrated and frictionless. If a tool can’t integrate directly with CRM, ERP or other core systems of record, its organizational impact will be limited.

Recent findings suggest that the enterprise technology stack is already crowded with companies deploying hundreds of apps and SaaS solutions. Many work independently, disconnected from the disparate app ecosystem surrounding companies major and small. Adding newly introduced AI tools to this mix has limited impact and can even create more work for employees. Effective AI adoption that justifies AI spend will go beyond tools that answer questions or generate generic content. It will involve AI solutions that can proactively identify opportunities, recommend actions and even execute work. ​.

For example, in marketing, where AI ad spending alone will top $32 billion in 2026, effective AI adoption could mean onboarding a solution that detects campaign performance complications, identifies underappreciated opportunities across a campaign or helps implement improvements to existing campaign collateral.

To maximize AI’s impact, invest in tools that make this possible and clarify the human element. Clearly define when AI can act independently, when approval is required and when humans must take the lead. ​.

Combining the right tools with the right purpose in structured workflows, with clear roles and responsibilities, is the best way to invest in AI that gets work done.

Industry observers note that AI is only as useful as the information and context it can access. Without clean, unified and reliable data, outputs can be inaccurate, inconsistent or disconnected from business priorities. Before making significant AI investments, smart enterprises will focus on organizing the technology they already have, connecting systems and simplifying workflows so AI can operate within business realities.​.

Focus on infrastructure that connects AI to relevant business data, organizational knowledge and workflows while respecting role-based permissions and account-level boundaries.​.

It has been revealed that understandably, security is foundational to these efforts. It can’t be bolted on later or retroactively applied. A governed environment, or “sandbox,” is a good place to start. Here, businesses can define what AI can access, what actions it can take and when it needs human approval.​.

Industry observers note that boosting productivity is great, but it shouldn’t come at the expense of data security or privacy. Clear accountability, auditability and oversight help businesses scale AI without losing control over sensitive data or consequential decisions.​.

It has been revealed that customers aren’t inherently impressed by a company’s AI strategy, and neither are boards or shareholders. Everyone is looking for results.

That’s why the competitive advantage comes from how well organizations connect AI to their data, people, processes and business goals. It’s the product of organizations that build the right foundation, enabling AI to do the right work with the right context and under the right controls.

Investing in these fundamentals may not make headlines, but it’s the AI infrastructure bet that smart enterprises are making to deliver lasting business value.​.

What Tom Gardner Said About Days Like This

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By The Motley Fool Team – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 10:49AM EST.
  • It has been revealed that if a glance at your portfolio this morning made you wince, the broad market shares the blame.
  • Back in September, Tom Gardner sat down to record his sixth Quarterly Call, and he spent a good chunk of it on days like this one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By The Motley Fool Team – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 10:49AM EST.

It has been revealed that if a glance at your portfolio this morning made you wince, the broad market shares the blame. The S&P 500 fell about 2.5% and the Nasdaq dropped more than 3.5%. The CBOE Volatility Index, often called Wall Street's fear gauge, jumped about 20%. If you own a lot of growth stocks, your account probably fell harder than the broad market.

Back in September, Tom Gardner sat down to record his sixth Quarterly Call, and he spent a good chunk of it on days like this one. He didn't predict today. Tom doesn't make market calls, and he gently scolds people who make spectacular ones. Instead, he explained why a drop like this shouldn't catch a Fool off guard, and what to do when one comes. Five ideas from his call are worth rereading before you touch the sell button.

It has been revealed that tom reminded us that the S&P 500 has historically fallen 10% about once a year. He called a pullback of 10% to 15% normal. Think of it as the toll you pay for decades of stock market returns.

He also argued the odds of a pullback were higher than usual when he recorded the call. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were trading 10% to 30% above their typical historical valuation ranges. When stocks are priced for good news, it takes less bad news to knock them down.

In a recent development, and he warned that when the index falls, the high-growth, high-beta stocks many Fools own tend to fall further. High beta means a stock swings harder than the market in both directions. This morning followed his script, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq down about a percentage point more than the S&P 500. If your portfolio is down more than the index today, your stocks are behaving the way Tom said they would.

Recent findings suggest that "Emotional reactivity is the enemy of wealth creation," Tom remarked. A red day tempts you to make a dramatic move, like selling everything or backing up the truck.

According to recent reports, tom's alternative is incrementalism. Buy and sell in stages, and recheck your thesis at every step. His example came from Hidden Gems, which sold 15% of its CrowdStrike (CRWD -5.87%) position in the weeks before the call. Tom said the team didn't expect calamity for the business. The stock looked richly priced, so HG took some cash off the table and kept the rest of its position.

Recent findings suggest that tom argued that moving in steps builds conviction. Each partial sale makes you rethink your reasons, and the rethinking can get you out of a bad position sooner than an all-or-nothing standoff in your head. If you feel the urge to do something before the holiday, do a small something.

Tom's first recommendation for this market was to pair higher-quality companies with lower return expectations. He used Costco (COST -0.15%) to show what he means.

He thinks Costco could deliver about 10% a year plus a small dividend. Over a decade, such a pace turns $10,000 into roughly $27,000. Tom admitted a return like Costco's sounds dull to anyone who's seen a stock do 2.7 times its money in six months. So he asked members to picture Costco handing them about 10% a year for the next decade, and to decide honestly whether those returns would satisfy them. Your answer, he stated, sets the frame for how you invest going forward.

Industry observers note that lower-quality companies carrying high expectations pose the opposite danger. Tom warned they can fall 50%, 70%, or 90% and never recover. If one of those becomes one of your largest positions, it can be "quite damaging to your pursuit of financial freedom," he said. He recommended keeping steady ballast in your portfolio. Ballast is the heavy weight low in a ship's hull that keeps the ship steady in rough water.

Industry observers note that tom reaffirmed a core Foolish principle. Own 50 or more companies, and keep each for more than five years on average.

Sources indicate that his reminder of why came from a stock he owns. Rocket Lab (RKLB -7.87%) had run up to $150 a share and then been cut in half by the time of the call. Tom still believes in the business, but he called a swing of that size a reminder of "the importance of having a diversified portfolio.".

Sources indicate that even this morning, not everything fell. The small-cap Russell 2000 was up about half a percent while the Nasdaq slid.

Industry observers note that tom's final action step was about your household, and it may matter most on a day like today. He suggested a family exercise. Figure out how cheaply you could live for a month and still enjoy your life. Then ask how big your emergency fund should be. Would six months of expenses be enough, or would you sleep better with nine or 12? If your family gathers for Thanksgiving tomorrow, you'll have everyone at one table to talk it through.

It has been revealed that his goal is to simulate a recession, a market decline, or a job change before any of them shows up. "Taking the step to improve the sustainability of a high-quality life is vastly more significant and notable than squeezing out extra percentage points of returns, particularly in a richly priced market," he said.

A household with its bills covered and cash in reserve can treat a falling market as a sale. Tom described investors who get through a 20% or even 40% decline comfortably. They keep a cash position on the side and put it to work in their favorite companies at lower prices. In a reply to members in the call's comments section, Tom mentioned his own cash position sits in the 10% to 15% range.

According to recent reports, tom closed the first section of his call with a line from his father, who created the Potential Growth Indicator you'll find on our site. After a long, happy day, when the Gardner kids asked to stay up late, their dad would say, "Tomorrow's another day." Tom offered his dad's advice to investors who try to cram every win into today. It works just as well for losses.

It has been revealed that this week, tomorrow is literally another day. U.S. stock markets are closed for Thanksgiving, and Fools get a break from the ticker. A bad morning is one morning, and Fools invest for decades.

Sources indicate that the wealth destruction in Nvidia has been swift and brutal. The company, which abruptly lost founder-CEO Jensen Huang before he was abruptly brought back, is scrambling amid potential sanctions violations, and faces competitive threats from all angles.

Still, it just reported strong Q3 earnings, with revenue up over 100% year over year. On a trailing-earnings basis, Nvidia now looks like one of the cheapest stocks in the S&P 500. Does that make it a buy below $160?

Nvidia's latest earnings report was quite strong. It had revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year prior. The business was firing on all cylinders through the end of October by selling computer chips for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

According to recent reports, investors are completely ignoring prior numbers and are worried about the potential chaos that could ensue from Huang's abrupt departure and then return. Interim CEO Colette Kress noted everything was business as usual with Nvidia, projecting revenue to grow 75% next fiscal year, which would likely bring Nvidia's sales to around $750 billion.

Sources indicate that some short-term milestones for the business will be stabilizing Huang as CEO during a tough time for the sector and proving there is a pipeline of buyers from across the AI sector lining up to buy. If Nvidia can maintain earnings momentum in the quarters ahead, that will be great news for the stock.

Sources indicate that jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

On a multi-year horizon, there are a few items investors worry about, and any investor buying the dip should consider them today.

In a recent development, first are the potential sanction violations in selling to China. The public does not know the full story of what Huang or Nvidia knew about selling computer chips that would evade Chinese sanctions from the U.S. government, but if they did know, there could be a massive penalty for the business.

There is also a new investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) into Nvidia's accounting practices, which could call into question the business's true earnings power.

Sources indicate that from a competitive standpoint, many companies are trying to dethrone Nvidia's chip lead. There are direct competitors in chip design, such as Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom, as well as Nvidia's own customers, like Alphabet and Amazon, designing their own chips for data centers.

According to recent reports, nvidia's revenue is growing rapidly today, but its dominant position in chipmaking for AI looks like it is ending, which could mean trouble for its long-term profitability. Investors should not disregard these facts when looking at Nvidia stock as a potential buy-the-dip candidate.

It has been revealed that nvidia now trades at a trailing price-to-earnings ratio (P/E) of 16.5. If its growth rate continues next fiscal year as management expects right now, the stock is likely trading well below a forward P/E of 10.

Quantitatively, Nvidia is one of the cheapest stocks on the market today -- that is, if you believe the numbers are durable.

According to recent reports, right now, Nvidia shares look incredibly cheap based on its near-term growth prospects. Cynics are concerned about long-term manufacturer culture, whether AI is a bubble, and Nvidia losing market share to latest competitors.

If the AI infrastructure build-out continues, Nvidia will likely do well by selling its cutting-edge chips to customers at a premium price. This is why its operating margin has grown to 66% over the last 12 months.

Sources indicate that however, if Nvidia loses its lead in AI chips, it will see lower demand for its products and lower selling prices, resulting in lower revenue and profit margins. This could be a double hit to earnings, making the seemingly cheap forward P/E look much more expensive five years from now.

For Noah, these changes require us to put the boundaries of our client acquisition, product suitability, and the servicing entity into practice in our actual operations in each market. We arranged our business strictly in line with the regulatory requirements that apply in Mainland China and international, respectively, and our international business relies more on local licensed entities to serve eligible clients. These adjustments to our business model are comprehensive. Although we begin planning and responding several months in advance, they still bring certain challenge to our revenue and profit in the short term. Even so, judging by the results, our new business remains stable, and we have delivered non-GAAP profitability for the 64th consecutive quarter since our live listing. On that basis, management is overall satisfied with this quarter's operating results. On the numbers, first quarter net revenue was RMB 509 million, down 19.6% year-over-year and down 17.9% sequentially.

It has been revealed that operating profit was RMB 64 million, down 62.8% year-over-year, while the operating margin was 12.6%. The sequential decline in net revenue was mainly driven by lower performance-based income, carry fell 77.2% sequentially, mainly due to market volatility. Excluding performance-based income, net revenue was basically flat sequentially, down only about 1%, which reveals that our business is resilient in the face of the policy shocks and the model adjustments. On the profit side, revenue declined while expenses increased, so operating profit fell sequentially. However, the increase in expenses was largely non-recurring, including onetime compensation of about RMB 35 million from our proactive adjustment of the relevant teams in Mainland China as well as a reduction in government subsidies.

In a recent development, over the longer term, labor costs continue to decline, but as the organizations becomes linear, there will still be one-time compensation in the coming quarters. Excluding these one-time factors, our operating margin would be 23.4% instead. Going forward, our focus is to actively develop more new channels and new markets and gradually build recurring revenue while controlling our own operating costs and improving efficiency. Our CFO later on will explain the financial figures in more detail. Next, I will report separately on our international business and our Mainland China business. On the international business, we expand our eligible clients through local teams and partners. At period end, International registered clients grew 10.7% year-over-year.

Net revenue was RMB 229 million, flat from the previous quarter, accounting for about 45% of the group's net revenue. More noteworthy is new net revenue. The international contribution was about RMB 88 million, accounting for about 2/3 of the group's new net revenue on the same basis, and it came from diverse sources, not limited to any single product. This demonstrates that our international business is supported by existing revenue with multiple new source contributing at the same time. As of the end of September, all this actively managed assets under -- stood at USD 6.6 billion, up 10.7% year-over-year and also higher than at the end of the second quarter.

Our business build-out in the U.S. and Japan continues to advance. As of third quarter, net revenue was RMB 82.2 million, down 43.8% year-over-year, mainly due to the decline in one-off insurance distribution commissions. While recurring service fee grew about 11% year-over-year, Gopher's net revenue was RMB 36.6 million, down 22.4% year-over-year. We will continue to actively expand client channels and improve the quality of service to existing clients, expand comprehensive services such as family legacy planning, and track the ongoing conversation of newly raised funds. As our business model adjusts, we are also streamlining the organization. At the end of the third quarter, the group's headcount was about 70% lower than at the end of the second quarter.

Industry observers note that in the past, fund managers often asked us how many RMs Noah has and how many more we would add any year? This was a reasonable question in the past because the wealth management industry used to grow mainly by adding RMs. But today, we are committed to building Noah into a platform open to RMs around the world. Today, growth is measured not only by the individual productivity of any RMs, but by whether the overall strength of the platform can attract and empower more client acquisition channels and clients. Our goal is not to simply layer technology on top of the traditional business, but to achieve a full transformation into an AI-native tech giant.

We are now fully extending our core capabilities in global products, investment research, intelligent technology, and compliance operations to RMs and partners, supporting each party to operate within its own licensing and compliance framework. On front-end service, we have built a 3-layer collaborative system: First, empowering RMs with digital tools to deepen client service; second, having the AI plus wealth management team handle day-to-day standardized service; and third, using the technology to support the expansion of the external ecosystem. On this basis, our client acquisition network now fully covers our own RMs, our partners, EAMs, and IFAs on the Nexus platform and business partner among other channels. Partners expand their clients locally within the group committed debt and the relevant international entities provide services. We are also actively expanding our business partner network. Individual and institutional business partners signed today number more than 100 with the relevant license personnel providing regulated professional services. Beyond business partners, we have also signed with 27 professional partner institutions, including 10 IFAs and 17 EAMs. Singapore is the first model site, where we are validating this approach.

We acquired clients through local events, client referrals, and partner expansions with the AI Plus wealth management team handling day-to-day service, senior ROM and the management team took part in serving key clients, while licensed personnel are responsible for compliance review and investment recommendations. According to the Singapore team's operating statistics as of the end of September, the asset bought by these channels -- these 3 channels, namely business partners, IFAs, and partners together account for about 48% of new AUM on that basis. The AI + Wealth Management department contributes about 65% of the revenue while also handling about 90% of client service work.

AUM under Singapore office have grown from less than USD 100 million at launch to about USD 429 million at the end of the third quarter, and the business reached monthly profitability in July. How Legacy Data Pipelines Become A Liability When AI Moves From Chat To Action

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that prashanthi Kolluru is the founder of KloudPortal.
  • In enterprise data engineering initiatives, I’ve noticed an often-overlooked pattern: a data pipeline can be judged successful simply because it runs as expected.
  • Sources indicate that this is becoming increasingly significant as enterprises move from AI assistants that retrieve information to agents that execute tasks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that prashanthi Kolluru is the founder of KloudPortal. Helping global capability centers (GCCs) hire product-ready engineering pods.

In enterprise data engineering initiatives, I’ve noticed an often-overlooked pattern: a data pipeline can be judged successful simply because it runs as expected. Data moves between systems, scheduled jobs complete, reports are delivered and the business keeps operating smoothly. Yet the same pipeline may rely on assumptions about data freshness, transformation logic, quality and business rules that become challenging to manage as requirements evolve.​.

Sources indicate that this is becoming increasingly significant as enterprises move from AI assistants that retrieve information to agents that execute tasks. An AI agent operating within an enterprise workflow may use incorrect information to update records, initiate processes or influence business decisions without anyone realizing it.​.

This shift has prompted me to examine more closely the weaknesses that may have been manageable in traditional analytics environments but become more critical when AI is integrated into operational workflows.

Five areas deserve particular attention before organizations extend AI agents into consequential workflows.

It has been revealed that A pipeline that refreshes data overnight may be perfectly adequate for a historical sales report. It can be unsuitable for an agent making decisions that depend on current inventory, account balances or order status.

The risk depends on the business decision, not simply on how old the data is. A delay of several hours may have little impact on one workflow and materially change the outcome of another.

In a recent development, technology leaders should define acceptable data freshness for each AI use case. Some workflows may need event-driven updates; others may work with scheduled processing. Rebuilding every pipeline for real-time delivery is rarely necessary. The goal is to match data availability to the consequences of acting on it.

Recent findings suggest that legacy pipelines often rely on scripts and mappings that embed source-specific assumptions and business rules. When engineers introduce a upcoming system or data source, they may need to modify multiple parts of the pipeline and retest downstream dependencies.

This becomes harder as AI agents need information from more enterprise systems and business context changes more frequently.

Metadata-driven pipeline architecture offers one way to reduce this maintenance burden. Source mappings, transformation rules, validation checks and load configurations can be managed as metadata that a reusable framework interprets. This can make changes easier to manage than repeatedly modifying hard-coded procedures.

Metadata alone, however, does not guarantee flexibility. Business rules still need clear ownership, version control and testing. Otherwise, an organization simply moves its complexity from code into configuration.

Sources indicate that A missing field or duplicate record in a dashboard may be noticed during a review. The same defect, consumed by an AI agent, could influence a subsequent workflow before a person examines the underlying data.

Sources indicate that consider customer records that use inconsistent identifiers across systems. An agent combining those records could associate an instruction with the wrong account if the pipeline fails to resolve the inconsistency.

In a recent development, validation therefore needs to go beyond checking whether a pipeline completed successfully. Teams should test completeness, uniqueness, relationships between records, acceptable ranges and relevant business rules. Where checks fail, the system should flag or quarantine affected data rather than silently passing it downstream.

The appropriate controls depend on the use case, but the principle is consistent: successful data movement is not proof of trustworthy data.

When an AI-assisted workflow produces an unexpected result, teams need to establish which source records were used, how those records were transformed and which business definitions applied at the time.

It has been revealed that that investigation becomes difficult when dependencies are undocumented, transformations are scattered across scripts or data definitions differ between systems. Without reliable lineage, teams may struggle to reproduce an outcome or identify where an error entered the pipeline.

In a recent development, organizations should maintain traceable data flows, versioned transformations and monitoring that connects pipeline failures to downstream use cases. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework can also help teams structure their approach to identifying, assessing and managing AI-related risks.

For workflows with significant business consequences, treat the ability to reconstruct the data path as an operational requirement, not merely a documentation exercise. ​.

A pipeline may deliver accurate account information to an agent, but access to that information should not automatically authorize the agent to initiate a payment, change a customer record or approve a transaction.

These are separate decisions: what data a system can read, what actions it can perform and which actions require human approval.

It has been revealed that as organizations connect agents to enterprise applications, they should define permissions around specific operations, use appropriate controls for higher-risk actions and retain audit trails of what the agent accessed and did. Access policies should apply to the agent’s identity and the workflow it operates within, not simply to the data source.

Data engineering and AI governance need to work together here. A well-governed pipeline cannot compensate for unrestricted action permissions, just as a tightly controlled agent cannot make unreliable data trustworthy. ​.

Industry observers note that modernizing a legacy data environment does not necessarily mean replacing every pipeline or moving every workload to real-time processing. It starts with understanding which data feeds support AI workflows and what can happen when those feeds are delayed, incomplete or incorrect.

In a recent development, can technology leaders assess those pipelines against five practical questions: Is the data fresh enough for the decision? Are transformations understandable and maintainable? Are quality failures detected before the data is used? Can you reconstruct the source and transformation history? Are data permissions and agent action permissions clearly separated?

Enterprises should avoid treating AI readiness as a separate layer added on top of existing data infrastructure. Pipeline design, maintenance and governance will influence what AI agents can safely do with enterprise information.

Organizations should examine these foundations early in AI planning rather than discover their limitations after agents become embedded in critical workflows. Modernization should reflect the business consequences of each use case and give AI agents a dependable basis for action.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

Sources indicate that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly crucial sources of transaction revenue, while the firm has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

Industry observers note that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

—With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

Cross-Functional Collaboration Is Fashion’s Fresh Competitive Advantage

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (863 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Maximilien Abadie, Deputy CEO and a member of the Executive Committee, Lectra.
  • Recent findings suggest that ​Speed and creativity have always been defining features of the fashion industry.
  • Companies that create the digital and cultural infrastructure to support cross-functional collaboration make it possible to unify workflows, anticipate challenges earlier and share data for faster, better decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maximilien Abadie, Deputy CEO and a member of the Executive Committee, Lectra.

Recent findings suggest that ​Speed and creativity have always been defining features of the fashion industry. In a climate marked by fragmentation and continuing volatility, accelerating time to market and achieving the all-key five R’s (right place, right product, right price, right quantities and right consumer) have become less about moving faster at individual stages and more about improving how information is shared and decisions are made across the value chain.

Companies that create the digital and cultural infrastructure to support cross-functional collaboration make it possible to unify workflows, anticipate challenges earlier and share data for faster, better decisions. This transforms the way a organization creates, manufactures and sells their products. ​.

According to recent reports, every product that makes it to market is shaped by contributions from hundreds of different individuals, many of whom do not speak the same language or share a common perspective. The linear, step-by-step approach to collection development—design followed by development, then production and ending with marketing, merchandising and e-commerce—struggles to provide the agility needed to respond quickly to the dynamism that characterizes this industry.

It has been revealed that when design, production and sales teams work as separate entities, each with their own tools, data and objectives, decision-making is slower and inefficiencies are greater. A feasibility glitch discovered in production could have been identified at the development stage. Consumer insights gathered during the marketing phase are not passed on to creative teams. These disconnects can result in missed sales opportunities, excess inventory and frustrated customers. ​.

Cross-functional collaboration supported by shared data contributes to greater resilience, innovation and growth. Research shows that cross-functional, team-focused transformations can drive a 30% increase in efficiency. When information flows freely across an interconnected value chain, decisions happen faster, errors are identified earlier and fewer resources are wasted.

One of the most tangible benefits of data-based collaboration is its impact on time to market, which remains a critical challenge for global fashion brands. While some fashion players can develop and launch products in a matter of days, others still operate on timelines of six to nine months. Closing this gap requires rethinking product development from the earliest creative stages and ensuring continuity of information across the entire product life cycle.

Beyond improving collaboration, these solutions help preserve and scale expertise by making institutional knowledge, technical know-how and historical product data accessible across the organization. Along with accelerating onboarding and decision-making, this helps brands ensure that valuable expertise is retained and leveraged across generations of teams.

Recent findings suggest that data-based collaboration requires a shared infrastructure capable of integrating multiple functions and partners. Solutions embedded with AI and digitalization are the key enablers of this transformation. While product life cycle management (PLM) solutions remain essential for product data management, governance and life cycle visibility, a new generation of AI-enabled product development solutions is emerging to support the day-to-day workflow of bringing a product from concept to production.

By bringing together internal teams, as well as a brand’s global network of suppliers, subcontractors and partners, these solutions ensure that all stakeholders are aligned and working from the same up-to-date information. Companies can capture and communicate data on designs, tech packs, materials, costs, timelines and suppliers in a common framework that cross-functional teams can rely on as products progress.

When each team member has a 360-degree vision of the product in its journey, there are fewer surprises and improved coordination.

The case for shared data infrastructure becomes even more urgent in light of upcoming traceability and sustainability regulations. The Digital Product Passport (DPP), part of the European Union’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation, will require products sold in the EU in 2027 to carry structured, standardized product information. Even in the early phase of implementation, which will be a minimal, simplified version of the digital product passport, companies will be expected to provide data on material composition, origin, carbon footprint, supply chain traceability, recyclability, care, durability and chemical compliance.

Recent findings suggest that compliance will require alignment across the full product cycle. While the first phase will most likely only require supply chain traceability up to Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers, adopting a digital traceability approach that starts with the original fibers that will eventually be used in garments and other products provides the foundation for visibility across all tiers of the supply chain. Artificial intelligence is a key enabler of this tracing technology. It continuously monitors transactions to detect inconsistencies or fraudulent claims, enabling brands to move from theoretical commitments to proven actions. Companies that build this infrastructure now will be positioned to leverage transparency as a competitive advantage.

Collaborative solutions are reshaping how work is organized, executed and experienced. Beyond enabling basic communication, they support new ways of working that emphasize shared visibility and consistency across teams. In a business environment increasingly characterized by volatility, complexity and rapid change, these platforms are becoming an important enabler for companies seeking to operate more efficiently and quickly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Sources indicate that glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

Industry observers note that “For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

It has been revealed that “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

It has been revealed that the most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Recent findings suggest that ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

Sources indicate that the 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

Recent findings suggest that of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

Robinhood Markets vs. Toast: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 11:01AM EST.
  • Investors choosing between Robinhood Markets (HOOD -5.98%) and Toast Inc.
  • Robinhood changed how individual investors access the stock market, while Toast provides the digital backbone for modern eateries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 11:01AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Robinhood Markets ›.

Investors choosing between Robinhood Markets (HOOD -5.98%) and Toast Inc. (TOST -3.19%) must weigh high-growth retail finance against specialized restaurant technology. Both companies are disrupting traditional service models to capture massive digital markets.

Robinhood changed how individual investors access the stock market, while Toast provides the digital backbone for modern eateries. Both businesses benefit from the shift toward digital-first financial interactions. This comparison examines their growth trajectories and valuations to help you decide which stock fits your 2027 goals.

Robinhood Markets provides a global platform for retail brokerage, cryptocurrency, and digital banking. Its platforms allow 28.7 million funded customers to trade equities and options. Key partners include SIG for derivatives trading and Morningstar Inc. (MORN +0.80%) for investment research. As one of the more prominent financial stocks, the company is actively diversifying its revenue streams through acquisitions like Bitstamp. It also collaborates with liquidity providers such as Virtu Financial inc. (VIRT -3.14%) for trading execution. These strategic relationships help the firm provide a seamless experience for its growing user base.

Industry observers note that in FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $4.5 billion, marking a significant growth rate of approximately 51.6% compared to the prior year. This follows a strong performance in FY 2024 where revenue was close to $3.0 billion. The company reported net income in 2025 of roughly $1.9 billion. This resulted in a net margin of around 42%, which measures the portion of revenue remaining as profit after all expenses. The upward trend in profitability highlights the company's focus on scaling its operations efficiently while adding fresh products like futures trading.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 1.3x. This ratio demonstrates how much debt a company uses to finance its assets relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts, is also roughly 1.3x. Free cash flow, which is cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures, reached nearly $1.6 billion. This liquidity provides the firm with flexibility for future acquisitions or further research and development initiatives into automated advisory services.

According to recent reports, toast sells a specialized technology platform for the restaurant and retail sectors, combining software, payment processing, and hardware. The manufacturer serves approximately 189,000 locations, ranging from small cafes to large enterprise chains. It also provides payroll processing and working capital loans through strategic bank partnerships. Many tech stocks seek to dominate a single niche, and Toast has achieved this within the restaurant community. By integrating all aspects of a restaurant's digital needs, the company creates a high level of customer loyalty. This integrated approach makes it difficult for competitors to displace its services.

In a recent development, in FY 2025, revenue reached close to $6.2 billion, representing a year-over-year increase of approximately 24%. This is an increase from the almost $5.0 billion in revenue generated during FY 2024. The tech giant reported a net income of roughly $342.0 million for the period. This produced a net margin of about 5.6%, which reflects the percentage of revenue kept as profit after accounting for all costs. This positive net income marks a significant improvement over the net loss reported in FY 2023, showing the business model is reaching a profitable scale.

Industry observers note that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, indicating the company carries no debt. Its current ratio is approximately 2.8x, suggesting a strong ability to cover near-term obligations with liquid assets. Free cash flow reached about $608 million for the year. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 36.6% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement. Even so, the lack of debt provides a clean financial profile for continued geographic expansion.

Robinhood Markets faces intense regulatory and litigation risks from agencies like the SEC and FINRA. Changes to rules regarding payment for order flow or the classification of cryptocurrencies could disrupt its core business model. Additionally, the company is highly sensitive to market volatility and interest rate changes. It also relies on third-party providers like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN -5.88%) for cloud infrastructure. Cybersecurity vulnerabilities at these third-party vendors pose significant operational and reputational risks if customer data is compromised.

Toast is currently facing a lawsuit from the Federal Trade Commission alleging deceptive pricing in customer contracts. The business also depends heavily on a limited number of payment processors and a single bank partner for its lending programs. Furthermore, the firm faces supply chain vulnerabilities for its hardware components from international manufacturers. Managing rapid growth has also placed strain on its internal accounting and IT systems. Failure to integrate acquired technologies effectively could lead to operational mistakes and a loss of customer satisfaction.

Toast appears to be the more conservatively priced option because its Forward P/E, based on future earnings estimates, and its P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months, are lower than those for Robinhood.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Robinhood introduced no-cost stock trading to the masses when it debuted last decade, raking in retail clients and sparking a move industrywide to mostly $0 commission trading for equities. The key to its strength is a simple, intuitive app that makes trading accessible, avoiding the complexity of trading platforms designed for professionals. That has the average age of a customer in the mid-30s, well below other brokerages.

Its appeal to traders resulted in a record third quarter of fiscal 2026, with Robinhood posting its highest-ever revenue of $1.42 billion, up 12% from the year-ago period, and net income of $468 million, down $98 million from 2025. The firm sees agentic trading, which only about 1% of customers utilize now, as a way to generate short-term growth, and the expected massive wealth transfer from the Baby Boom generation to younger adults as a long-term tailwind that should help establish its wealth management offerings.

For fiscal 2027, analysts foresee revenue of $6.88 billion, a rise of about 29% from 2026's expected final tally of $5.32 billion, with net income of around $2.7 billion, up 49%.

Toast, meanwhile, continues to add thousands of restaurants each quarter as that industry seeks a single platform to handle a myriad of tasks, like employee scheduling, point-of-sale transactions, tip automation, back-office needs, loyalty programs, handling takeout orders, and personalized marketing to customers.

It has been revealed that all that should bring in 2027 revenue of $8.89 billion, which would be a rise of about 19% from 2026's expected full-year sales of $7.49 billion. Net income next year should touch $732 million, up about $140 million from 2026.

Longer term, Toast management sees opportunities to expand into gas station convenience stores, since most are small businesses, and into sports and entertainment facilities.

So which stock is the better buy for 2027? Robinhood trades at a premium, and while revenue forecasts are good, a bearish stock market always reduces retail traders' interest in the market and trading volumes. That is a potential risk. Toast, meanwhile, has a formula that is driving fast growth in the highly fragmented restaurant industry, from high-end eateries to takeout breakfast joints. At a cheaper forward PP/E and P/S than Robinhood, it's likely the more profitable position to build.

#120341. Industry News: When Days Matter: Navigating The AI-Accelerated Exploit Lifecycle

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1072 w)
📖 Baca
