Industry News: When Days Matter: Navigating The AI-Accelerated Exploit Lifecycle

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1072 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eoin Keary Founder & CEO of Edgescan, an enterprise CTEM (Continuous Testing and Exposure Management platform) used by Fortune 500s.
  • Industry observers note that ​AI is fundamentally changing the velocity of the threat landscape, particularly the time between vulnerability discovery and weaponization.
  • Industry observers note that this creates a latest imperative: Security processes designed around periodic assessment and remediation must evolve to operate at the speed of continuous change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eoin Keary Founder & CEO of Edgescan, an enterprise CTEM (Continuous Testing and Exposure Management platform) used by Fortune 500s.

Industry observers note that ​AI is fundamentally changing the velocity of the threat landscape, particularly the time between vulnerability discovery and weaponization. Vulnerabilities that historically took months, or even up to a year, to become active exploits can now move into the wild within days. AI also expands the attack surface itself as organizations deploy AI systems and agents across their environments, including systems that may not be fully visible to security teams.​.

Industry observers note that this creates a latest imperative: Security processes designed around periodic assessment and remediation must evolve to operate at the speed of continuous change. They should consider a different approach to security that employs AI to manage data volume while retaining a human in the loop for critical decision making. In this way, their organizations can rise with the tide of AI-driven threats by purifying their cybersecurity data to ensure it remains manageable and actionable.​.

The fundamental challenge in vulnerability management has never been finding vulnerabilities but determining which findings represent genuine, actionable risk. Organizations must distinguish between false positives, vulnerabilities that are real but not exploitable and vulnerabilities that are exploitable but mitigated by other controls.​.

Only after those layers of validation can security teams determine which remaining vulnerabilities represent the greatest business risk and should be addressed first. AI threatens to amplify the existing “vulnerability noise” problem by dramatically increasing the volume of findings entering the security team’s workflow. The answer can’t be asking already-constrained security and development teams to manually process an increasingly powerful “firehose” of alerts.​.

Slowing down detection isn’t the answer. A better answer is to add a validation layer between detection and action. The value of continuous assessment is its ability to provide a more current view of the environment. Without validation, however, it just produces more noise, faster. This is especially important as AI accelerates both vulnerability discovery and vulnerability exploitation.

According to recent reports, the temptation to use AI to automate remediation and allow systems to patch vulnerabilities without human intervention is obvious.​ Yet autonomous remediation can introduce significant operational risk when an AI system lacks the business context necessary to understand the consequences of its actions. AI should be used to make security professionals “more bionic,” processing information, accelerating analysis and supporting decisions, while humans retain responsibility for critical remediation decisions.​.

Recent findings suggest that as for technical vulnerability data, it alone is insufficient to determine what an organization should fix first. Effective prioritization requires context about the affected asset, its criticality, its role in the business, its data flows and the potential consequences of exploitation. AI can help organizations apply and process this context at scale, but only if the underlying security data is accurate, validated and meaningful.

Sources indicate that for teams already buried in findings, the promise of less noise is appealing. The questions start when we discuss what adopting it involves. How much of their time will we need? Will it work with their existing tools? Will the findings arriving on their desks actually be any better?

Industry observers note that in conversations with customers and prospective clients, these are always understandable concerns. They’ve heard plenty of promises about making security simpler. They want to know how much work it’ll take to get started and how much work it’ll save them afterwards. Sending over a mountain of alerts and wishing the team good luck is a fairly generous interpretation of helping.

It has been revealed that providers need to be clear about who does the work. If we offer validated findings, the validation is our responsibility. It’s important to establish which findings are real and investigate exploitability and assess relevant controls before passing the results to the customer.

According to recent reports, trust is another hurdle. Fewer findings can sound suspicious when the industry has spent years presenting bigger numbers as evidence of a better job. Customers need to see why something has been ruled out or deprioritized, what testing supports that decision and what remains uncertain.

According to recent reports, “AI said so” isn’t an explanation I’d fancy taking into a board meeting. Show the evidence and let people challenge the conclusion.​.

In a recent development, privacy and operational security deserve direct answers. What data will the provider access, and where will it be processed? What testing is permitted, and who approved it? Clear boundaries, documented data handling and named responsibilities help customers assess this service properly. They shouldn’t need a detective to work out what they’re signing up for.

Recent findings suggest that yes, cost always comes up, but the subscription is only part of the calculation. Investigating false positives, chasing findings that can’t be reproduced and passing inconclusive tickets between teams all costs money. Those hours don’t become free because they’re missing from the procurement spreadsheet. Providers must demonstrate the reduction in effort for the client and explain the price they charge.

According to recent reports, the practical route is to start with a defined scope and agree what success looks like with security development and the budget owner. Measure the time spent investigating findings, the quality of evidence reaching developers and how rapidly confirmed risks receive attention. Make implementation manageable, work with existing systems and show the results. That gives each team a reason to support adoption.​​.

Organizations need greater visibility into their attack surface and a continuous understanding of what they’re trying to secure. Continuous assessment and visibility will become increasingly notable as the pace of vulnerability discovery and exploitation accelerates. However, continuous assessment inevitably creates more data, making validation and suppression of irrelevant or low-value findings increasingly important.

In a recent development, organizations should prioritize security approaches that continuously assess the environment while filtering, validating and contextualizing findings before they reach security and development teams. The ultimate objective isn’t to automate every security decision but to ensure that even as the volume of cybersecurity data grows exponentially, organizations can reduce that information to a manageable number of accurate, contextual and actionable risks.​.

In an AI-accelerated threat landscape, the organizations best positioned to respond will be those that can rise with the tide by purifying their cybersecurity data rather than drowning in it.​​.

The ongoing earnings season, Middle East tensions and buzz ahead of the U.S. midterm elections have been keeping investors busy. Further, worries about elevated artificial intelligence spending are weighing on investor sentiment.

Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Sources indicate that this week's first stock pick is Datadog, an AI-powered observability and security platform. The firm will announce its results for the third quarter on Nov. 4. Datadog is seeing strong demand for its offerings, thanks to cloud migration and rapid AI adoption. TipRanks' KPIs tool for DDOG indicates the growth in its customer base over the past few years amid increasing market penetration and growing adoption of its products.

Heading into Q3 FY26 earnings, Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda reiterated a buy rating on Datadog stock and raised his price target to $335 from $305. The analyst noted that industry checks and data indicate that infrastructure software demand is strengthening, with AI increasingly driving usage and growth.

Sources indicate that ikeda called Datadog and Atlassian his top picks, saying that companies that can show that AI is a tailwind to growth could see their valuation rerate, even at premium multiples. He added that the total addressable market for observability is growing faster than anticipated, driven by accelerated growth of enterprise AI and the rapid ramp of consumer AI agents.

The five-star analyst believes that focus will be on revenue growth, which he estimates to be 28.7% for Q3 FY26 versus the Street's consensus of 29.1%. Ikeda thinks that the market is underestimating the growth prospects of DDOG's security products. Meanwhile, he cautioned investors about concentration risk related to large customers.

"We think results will be supportive of our long-term thesis that Datadog is a strong share gainer in the rapidly expanding observability opportunity," said Ikeda.

According to recent reports, ikeda ranks No. 673 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 55% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.9%. See Datadog Statistics on TipRanks.

The next pick, semiconductor giant Nvidia, is also benefiting from AI-driven demand for its products. After attending Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reaffirmed a buy rating on NVDA stock with a price target of $300, calling it a top pick in the semiconductor space.

The five-star analyst said that the conference supported his thesis that Nvidia continues to effectively navigate bottlenecks in the supply chain, land/power/shell, and funding. In fact, Moore is "convinced that all 3 aspects are opportunities for NVDA.".

Sources indicate that while Nvidia's GTC Berlin offered no major updates, Moore noted the conference reflected that the company continues to add to its significant advantages heading into 2027. The analyst mentioned that Vera Rubin is gaining momentum, though details on next year's Rubin Ultra were lighter than expected.

With demand outpacing supply, Moore stated that focus is on closing the gap. In this regard, he highlighted the supply chain deals on substrate, packaging and testing. While the analyst continues to view TSMC 3 nm wafer supply as the biggest challenge, he expects it to ease over time.

Moore ranks No. 142 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.4%. See Nvidia Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Aerospace tech giant SpaceX recently confirmed solid third-quarter results, with its AI revenue surging to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the prior-year quarter.

Industry observers note that impressed by the results, Needham analyst Ryan Koontz reiterated a buy rating on SPCX stock with a price target of $250. Koontz highlighted that SpaceX's Q3 results significantly exceeded expectations, proving that the tech giant's vertically integrated business model is driving massive scale.

Furthermore, Koontz emphasized the 195.2% sequential growth in SpaceX's AI revenue, fueled by wholesale spot compute deals. He noted management's increasing focus on its AI strategy, given that it is optimistic about adding 10 gigawatts of incremental capacity during 2027.

"With increasing confidence on Starship re-use, we meaningfully increase our estimates," remarked Koontz.

The acquisition of smart-switch maker Deako expands distribution into upcoming home construction, establishing a multiyear product footprint across millions of planned housing units.

Management is tracking direct-to-consumer upgrade adoption, gross margin expansion, and progress toward cash flow positive operations.

As home automation evolves, the integrated plug-and-play platform provides a direct channel for hardware and recurring software upgrades. Unifying ceiling and wall connections establishes the infrastructure needed for future artificial intelligence (AI) services, room sensors, and safety monitoring in single-family homes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Democrats' midterm election win has put the artificial intelligence trade in question, as voters clearly expressed opposition to the rapid buildout of data centers. The stock market could remain volatile amid AI trade concerns, macro uncertainties, and geopolitical tensions.

Recent findings suggest that in this scenario, investors can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios to earn steady income. However, the extensive universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as these experts assign ratings after in-depth financial analysis.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Viper Energy (VNOM) is a subsidiary of Diamondback and owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests, primarily in the Permian Basin. The company reported upbeat third-quarter earnings, supported by recent acquisitions and continued development activity from Diamondback and third-party operators. Viper announced a base cash dividend of 50 cents per share for Q3 2026, payable on Nov. 19. Based on the base and variable dividends announced over the past 12 months, VNOM's dividend yield stands at 5.7%.

Following the Q3 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper Energy stock with a price target of $61. The analyst noted that the company delivered solid Q3 results, with production, including oil and natural gas liquids, exceeding both TD Cowen and consensus estimates.

The 5-star analyst highlighted that the key upgrade was the announcement of two royalty acquisitions for $809 million in cash, including deferred consideration, and $82 million of newly issued shares.

In a recent development, given the recently announced base dividend hike, Bilkoski expects Viper to direct incremental free cash flow toward buybacks. While the acquisitions increase leverage, the analyst believes that Viper has enough capacity for opportunistic buybacks.

Bilkoski noted that Viper has historically delivered one of the highest production per share growth profiles in his royalty coverage, but still trades at a notable discount to the royalty peer average and the manufacturer's historical FCF yield range. "In our view, its above-average growth warrants a higher valuation," said the analyst.

Bilkoski ranks No. 525 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.80%. See Viper Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

Industry observers note that exxon Mobil (XOM) reported robust Q3 2026 profits, as its U.S. refineries boosted production to capitalize on the high diesel fuel prices sparked by the conflict in the Middle East. The oil and gas giant announced a quarterly dividend of $1.07 per share, payable on Dec. 10, reflecting a 3.9% increase. This marks Exxon's 44th consecutive year of dividend increases. At an annualized dividend of $4.28 per share, XOM offers a yield of 2.53%.

Impressed by the Q3 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Exxon stock and raised his price target to $193 from $180 to reflect higher downstream earnings, with the expectation of increased mid-cycle margins.

Recent findings suggest that gabelman noted that the strength in Exxon's refining business continues to offset Middle East-related headwinds. He added that the manufacturer increased its ownership in LNG projects, which should reduce its Middle East concentration over time from 75% to 50% and lower the likelihood of diversification-focused mergers and acquisitions. Beyond LNG, Gabelman expects Exxon's growth in the 2030s to come from Guyana, Kashagan, Permian, and possibly Venezuela.

Gabelman noted that Exxon announced a dividend hike of nearly 4% and plans to maintain buybacks at $20 billion for 2027. "The decision to maintain reduces the pro-cyclicality nature of the buyback," remarked the analyst.

Industry observers note that gabelman ranks No. 347 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.90%. See Exxon Mobil Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Williams (WMB), which owns and operates energy infrastructure to deliver natural gas, reported strong third-quarter results. The firm declared a quarterly dividend of $0.525 per share, or $2.10 per share annualized, payable on Dec. 28. WMB offers a dividend yield of 3.09%.

Industry observers note that in reaction to the Q3 2026 results, CIBC analyst Robert Catellier reaffirmed a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $82. The analyst noted that Q3 results were essentially in line with expectations and reflected continued strength in execution across WMB's infrastructure portfolio.

Catellier remarked that Williams' Q3 performance was driven by higher transmission, storage, and power generation revenues, as well as contributions from the Momentum Midstream acquisition.

He noted that Williams maintained its full-year EBITDA guidance of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion. In fact, results are tracking toward the higher end of the guidance range, backed by contributions from recently completed projects and the Momentum Midstream deal. WMB continues to target long-term EBITDA compound annual growth rate of at least 11% through 2030.

Catellier expects WMB's long-term targets to be supported by incremental transmission and storage opportunities, including Transco's Southeast Supply Enhancement II project and an 84 MMcf/d expansion of the Garden Connector project.

Catellier ranks No. 667 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 9.60%. See Williams Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

  • Pity Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.34%) investors.
  • Once the hottest space stock on the market -- priced north of $225 per share after a very successful IPO -- shares of the space-and-AI giant have taken a hit as investors worry Elon Musk made a mistake when he bet the company on AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Rich Smith – Nov 25, 2026 at 11:03AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

Pity Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.34%) investors.

Once the hottest space stock on the market -- priced north of $225 per share after a very successful IPO -- shares of the space-and-AI giant have taken a hit as investors worry Elon Musk made a mistake when he bet the company on AI.

And that's not the only thing they're worried about.

SpaceX stock fell 7.4% through 10:45 a.m. ET Wednesday -- and has lost twice that so far in November. Now trading around $113 per share, SpaceX stock is worth significantly less than the $135 it IPO'd at, and is once again at risk of being labeled a broken IPO.

Part of the reason for that is growing investor unease at the cost of building an AI economy. But as I explained last week, investors are also growing nervous about what it might cost if Elon Musk forces SpaceX to buy his other tech company, Tesla (TSLA -6.10%).

As StreetInsider.com reports today, The Future Fund managing partner Gary Black is warning that SpaceX might need to pay a 25% premium to acquire Tesla. And in an all-stock deal, this might require SpaceX to increase its share count by 52% to create all the stock needed to pay for the purchase.

NASDAQ · As of 11:16 AM ET 11/25/26.

Sources indicate that believe it or not, though, that's the good news. That's the best-case scenario.

Industry observers note that last week, investment bank HSBC suggested that buying Tesla could actually cost SpaceX more than $500 a share -- not a "25% premium," but closer to 40%. And between that higher implied price and the falling value of SpaceX's own stock, buying Tesla today could require SpaceX to glitch not 52% more shares, but closer to 81% more shares.

Yes, you read that right. If Elon Musk proceeds with merging his two tech empires, the cost to SpaceX shareholders could be more than 80% stock dilution. No wonder they're upset.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 25, 2026 at 11:05AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than BrightSpring Health Services ›.

It has been revealed that on its third-quarter 2026 earnings c(BTSG -2.40%)all, held on Oct. 30, 2026, BrightSpring revealed total organization revenue increased 26% year over year to $4.2 billion while raising its full-year guidance for adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), a measure of core operating profitability. The healthcare services provider continues to scale its dual model of pharmacy solutions and provider services, showing that lower-cost care in patients' homes creates durable financial compounding.

Three key takeaways from management's comments highlight the long-term thesis.

In a recent development, specialty pharmacy revenue jumped 34% year over year, driven by limited distribution drugs (LDDs), which are medications restricted by manufacturers to select specialty pharmacies. It launched 19 branded LDDs through nine months of 2026, and they're producing more revenue in year one than last year's cohort.

Sources indicate that brightSpring brought its net debt leverage ratio down to 1.79 times adjusted EBITDA while generating $204 million in quarterly operating cash flow. It doesn't need massive acquisitions to compound, focusing instead on tuck-in mergers and acquisitions (M&A), which is the purchase or combination of smaller regional healthcare businesses.

The company absorbed a $200 million annual revenue drag from the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which is federal healthcare legislation modifying prescription drug reimbursement, in its home and community pharmacy segment. It didn't let that statutory headwind stall momentum, relying on technology upgrades in end markets like assisted living facilities (ALF) to restore profit growth.

Industry observers note that patient care continues shifting toward lower-cost home settings, and management is positioning its expanded network to capture that growing national demand. The company leverages scale across procurement, proprietary care coordination models, and automated administrative workflows to widen its operational advantage over smaller regional providers.

With leverage down and full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to between $850 million and $860 million, management expects its compound growth momentum to carry forward into next year.

10 stocks we like better than Floor & Decor ›.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, Floor & Decor (FND +1.78%) announced it's slowing newly introduced store openings next year while preserving its long-term expansion targets. Higher mortgage rates and sluggish housing turnover continue to weigh on massive-ticket home renovation spending across the industry. Adjusting capital deployment gives the business flexibility to protect cash flow and return money to shareholders until housing activity recovers.

Three key takeaways from management's comments highlight how the company looks to navigate this cycle.

Industry observers note that management is slowing warehouse openings to 10 to 15 locations in 2027, down from 20 locations in 2026, to align growth with depressed home sales. Rather than chasing rigid store count targets during a housing slump, the retailer is prioritizing capital returns and preserving high-quality real estate opportunities for when demand rebounds.

It has been revealed that sales to professional contractors, or Pros, accounted for 55% of third-quarter revenue as management expanded its supply house approach in stores. To deepen these trade relationships, the firm piloted a new loyalty program that rolls out nationwide in the first quarter of 2027.

Recent findings suggest that the retailer ended the quarter with $1.0 billion in unrestricted liquidity, which includes cash and credit capacity under its asset-based lending facility, or ABL facility, a line of credit secured by inventory and accounts receivable. Operating cash flow reached $485.3 million through nine months. That cash flow gives management room to fund internal initiatives and buy back $157.1 million of common stock.

Industry observers note that high mortgage rates pressure home improvement demand, yet store teams are focusing on expense control and supply chain efficiency. Direct sourcing and broad tile assortments support long-term market share growth.

Executives are watching fuel costs, gross margins, and contractor activity into 2027.

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest massive-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

Sources indicate that “A perfect day for him,” stated De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”.

It has been revealed that "What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX.

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

Sources indicate that in the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their newly introduced song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs.

In a recent development, “We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi mentioned. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”.

It has been revealed that cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

In a recent development, buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”.

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Recent findings suggest that kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW.

Sources indicate that the victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

Industry observers note that “Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against significant teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”.

According to recent reports, A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi mentioned. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a significant player for us.

It has been revealed that “I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”.

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

Industry observers note that “We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones noted. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most vital.”.
